We further identify a likelihood-separation stability condition that is necessary for any estimator to attain this rate and, under mild regularity conditions, sufficient for both maximum likelihood and method-of-moments estimators to attain it. We also study the regime in which the target accuracy vanishes together with the signal strength, and show that global localization and local refinement may be governed by different likelihood orders, leading to distinct statistical scales. Finally, we apply our framework to broad classes of algebraically structured latent-variable models, including additive-noise channels and exponential-family models.

papers.title: A Tensor Critical Threshold in Cubic Spherical Kernel Graphs
papers.abstract:
We identify a strong-detection transition within the critical scale for testing cubic spherical kernel graphs against $G(n,1/2)$. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent uniform points on $\mathbb S^{d-1}$. Conditional on these points, edges are independent, with connection probability \[
  \frac{1+\beta Z_{3,d}(\langle X_i,X_j\rangle)}{2}. \] Here $Z_{3,d}$ is the normalized cubic zonal harmonic, with multiplicity $N_{3,d}\sim d^3/6$. Assume $n\to\infty$, $d=d_n\to\infty$, $\beta=\beta_n$ with $|\beta|\le1$, and $n\le d^A$, with $A<\infty$ fixed. Write $r_n=n\beta^2/(N_{3,d}d)$. On the critical scale $r_n\to r\in(0,\infty)$, we identify the tensor variational threshold \[
  r_{\mathrm{tens}}
  :=\min_{0<q<1}\frac{-2\{\log(1-q)+q\}}{q^6}. \] For $0<r<r_{\mathrm{tens}}$, the log-likelihood ratio under the null admits an asymptotically Gaussian expansion in the signed triangle, and the total-variation distance converges to $2\Phi(r^{3/2}/2)-1$, where $\Phi$ is the standard normal distribution function. For $r>r_{\mathrm{tens}}$, the likelihood-ratio test is strongly consistent, although the centered signed triangle still has Gaussian fluctuations. In the strict regimes $r_n\to0$ and $r_n\to\infty$, total variation tends to zero and one, respectively, even when $\beta\to0$.

papers.title: On dimension of posets excluding a standard example
papers.authors: J\k{e}drzej Hodor, Piotr Micek, William T. Trotter
papers.abstract: We prove that for every integer $d \geq 3$, there exists $\alpha <1$ such that the maximum dimension of an $n$-element poset containing no standard example of order $d$ as an induced subposet is $\mathcal{O}_d(n^\alpha)$. For $d=3$, we obtain an upper bound $\mathcal{O}(n^{2/3}\log n)$, while we also construct a family of $S_3$-free posets with dimension $\Omega(n^{1/3}/\log n)$. The proofs were found by OpenAI's ChatGPT-6 Astra.

papers.title: Stochastic Gradient Leimkuhler-Matthews Integrator with Second Order Discretization Error
papers.authors: Xuda Ye, Yuliang Wang, Guang Lin, Cindy Xiangrui Kong
papers.abstract: Stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics (SGLD) has a discretization error of first order in the step size $h$, even with the full gradient. We study the stochastic gradient Leimkuhler-Matthews (SGLM) integrator, which has the same cost as SGLD, one stochastic gradient per step, and reuses each Gaussian vector in consecutive steps. With the full gradient, SGLM is the Leimkuhler-Matthews (LM) integrator, whose discretization error for the invariant distribution is of second order. For a potential strongly convex outside a ball, we prove the bound $\mathcal O(\frac{1}{Nh} + \Sigma^2 h^2 + h^4)$ on the mean square error (MSE) of time averages of SGLM over $N$ steps, where $\Sigma$ bounds the variance of the gradient noise. The proof uses a modified class that absorbs the non-Markovian part of SGLM. The discretization error enters this bound as $h^4$ and the MSE bound of SGLD as $h^2$, while a larger batch reduces only the term $\Sigma^2 h^2$ in both bounds. In Bayesian logistic regression on MNIST, SGLM has a smaller estimated MSE than SGLD. The coefficient of $h$ in the numerical bias of SGLM is given explicitly by the covariance of the gradient noise and the continuous Poisson equation. The coefficient for SGLD contains in addition the Hessian of the potential, which comes from the discretization error. Through Riesz representors, the coefficients of the numerical bias determine the coefficients of the Wasserstein-1 errors of SGLM and SGLD.

papers.title: Information Theory of Random Composition Trees
papers.authors: Doron Sivan, Weishun Zhong, Tankut Can, Mikhail Katkov, Misha Tsodyks
papers.abstract: Random composition trees model the hierarchical semantic structures of meaningful texts as a statistical ensemble generated by recursively splitting texts into coherent chunks. A recent study shows that different text types can be described by random composition trees with distinct branching factors, and that the entropy rates of these trees exhibit a similar dependence across text types as the entropy rates of the actual texts. Motivated by this correspondence, we analyze information-theoretic properties of this stochastic splitting model. First, we demonstrate that the entropy of random composition trees grows linearly with the root size, and we derive an analytical expression for the entropy rate as a function of the branching factor. Second, we prove that large trees exhibit typicality: with high probability, they belong to a typical set in which each tree is approximately equally likely. Our analysis reveals that the random composition tree model shares two key information-theoretic properties of language when modeled as a stationary and ergodic stochastic process: linear entropy growth and typicality.

papers.title: BBP Transition for Deformed Inhomogeneous Random Matrices
papers.authors: Ruohan Geng, Zhantao He, Dang-Zheng Liu, Guangyi Zou
papers.abstract: We study finite-rank deformations of inhomogeneous random symmetric/Hermitian matrices $H_N=(\sigma_{ij}W_{ij})_{i,j=1}^N$, whose variance profile satisfies $\sum_j\sigma_{ij}^2=1$. Writing $\sigma_N^*=\max_{i,j}\sigma_{ij}$ for the matrix sparsity parameter, we establish the BBP transition of outlier eigenvalues at the level of the law of large numbers in two regimes of moment conditions on $\{W_{ij}\}$: (1) under a uniform sub-Weibull bound with exponent $0<\alpha\le 2$ and the sharp assumption $\sigma_N^*(\log N)^{1/\alpha}\to 0$, the convergence holds almost surely; (2) under uniformly integrable $p$-th powers for some $p\ge 4$ and the sharp assumption $N(\sigma_N^*)^{p-2}=O(1)$, the convergence holds in probability. Our approach combines sharp norm estimates, fixed-degree polynomial isotropic laws, and a finite-dimensional resolvent equation.

papers.title: An Accurate Zeroth-Order Perturbation Theory for Solving Power-Law Potentials within the Framework of the Asymptotic Iteration Method
papers.authors: A. J. Sous, Ibsal Assi, Nasser Saad
papers.abstract: Spherically symmetric singular potentials have a wide range of applications, such as molecular and atomic physics. In this work, we present a zeroth-order perturbation theory for solving the Schr\"odinger equation within the framework of the asymptotic iteration method (AIM). We rely on exponential and hyperbolic potential ansatz substitutions, where the difference between the original and new potential is treated as a small perturbation. Each potential ansatz has a free parameter chosen small enough to give an accurate zeroth-order perturbative wave equation solution. This method avoids the oscillatory behavior observed in the asymptotic iteration solutions when applying the AIM to such problems. Finally, we illustrate our approach by solving a few problems, particularly potentials with quartic and sextic singularities. We compare our results with those obtained via other methods and find good agreement.

papers.title: On the existence of a spectral gap for ergodic Markov chains
papers.abstract: Characterizations are established regarding the existence of an $L^2$-spectral gap for ergodic (that is, irreducible, aperiodic, and positive) Markov chains on infinite state spaces. In particular, it is shown that the existence of an $L^2$-spectral gap is entirely determined by the behavior of the spectrum at 1. These results are applied in the analysis of a family of Markov chains constructed to show that the ergodic composition of two geometrically ergodic Markov kernels need not be geometrically ergodic.

papers.title: K\"ahler-Ricci Flow is Symplectic Deflation plus an Exact Symplectic Deformation
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that K\"ahler-Ricci flow on a Fano surface decomposes as a symplectic deflation along a plurianticanonical divisor plus an exact symplectic deformation in the divisor complement. We apply this decomposition to the study of certain projective bundles. We establish the optimal decay rate in the setting of Song, Sz\'ekelyhidi, and Weinkove for a family of toric metrics which match the cohomological profile of K\"ahler-Ricci flow. In doing so, we identify a $C^2$-obstruction to proving the optimal decay rate in the setting of ruled toric surfaces. We present these ideas as a new symplectic-topological approach to the study of K\"ahler-Ricci flow.

papers.title: On the long wave limit of the good Boussinesq equation
papers.abstract: We consider the good Boussinesq equation on the line. Sufficiently regular solutions are known to converge in the long wave limit to a pair of counterpropagating solutions to the Korteweg--de Vries equation. We prove that this convergence holds for solutions in $H^{-\frac12}$, the largest Sobolev space in which the good Boussinesq equation is well-posed. As part of our analysis, we revisit the well-posedness theory, proving new a priori estimates and a corresponding small data global well-posedness result.

papers.title: An example of a non-sofic hyperbolic group
papers.abstract: We construct a torsion-free, two-dimensional, word-hyperbolic group which is not sofic. Our construction builds on OpenAI's construction of a non-residually finite hyperbolic group, see OpenAI 252.

papers.title: Double shuffle and naive duality for multiple Dirichlet series
papers.abstract:
Multiple zeta values admit both iterated-sum and iterated-integral representations, giving rise to the stuffle, shuffle and duality relations. Although these relations are satisfied by many families of complex numbers, we show that multiple zeta values are essentially uniquely determined by the double shuffle relations within a natural class of geometric multiple Dirichlet series.
  We then study geometric multiple Dirichlet series satisfying the shuffle relations and a duality relation. Under suitable analytic assumptions, we show that such dualities arise from differentiable involutions. We also use this framework to derive linear functional relations among multiple polylogarithms. Finally, we consider a more naive notion of multiple Dirichlet series and discuss the restrictions imposed by the stuffle relations, together with a conjecture on the uniqueness of multiple zeta values in this setting.

papers.title: The big cactus group, invariant tensors, and rectangular tableaux
papers.authors: Gabriel Frieden, Pavlo Pylyavskyy, Leonid Rybnikov
papers.abstract: The cactus group acts on tensor products of crystals and, through Bender--Knuth involutions, on semistandard Young tableaux. We show that the big cactus group $J'_n=\pi_1^{\mathfrak S_n}(\overline M_{0,n}(\mathbb R))$, $n\ge3$, is obtained from the cactus group by imposing $n-1$ Dynkin-reversal relations, which say that conjugation by the full reversal acts on the Bender--Knuth generators by the Dynkin diagram automorphism; the quotient map is induced by forgetting the distinguished marked point. We give a second presentation, in which these relations are replaced by the requirement that every reduced word for the longest element of $\mathfrak S_n$ adapted to an orientation of $A_{n-1}$ represents the full reversal. These relations also hold on rectangular tableaux, where every adapted reduced word therefore acts as evacuation, and on invariant tensors: for finite normal crystals of any complex semisimple Lie algebra, the cactus action on invariants factors through $J'_n$. We prove the latter combinatorially in type $A$ and in general via Gaudin eigenline coverings. Haiman's promotion relation follows from a single adapted-word relation, but for $n\ge4$ it is strictly weaker than the whole family.

papers.title: Interior caustics and rigidity near noncircular ellipses
papers.abstract: We prove local rigidity near every fixed noncircular ellipse from integrable rational caustics in an arbitrary nonempty open rotation interval $I\subset(0,1/2)$. For each fixed $r>11/2$ and bound on the $H^r$ norm of the elliptic graph displacement, every sufficiently $C^1$-small positively curved perturbation admitting such caustics at all rational rotations in $I$ is an ellipse. A fixed $C^6$ bound may replace the Sobolev bound, with $C^1$ smallness retained. The caustic hypothesis can be restricted to a suitably chosen sequence of rational rotations in $I$ with any prescribed rational $\rho_*\in I$ as its unique accumulation point, together with finitely many supplementary rotations in $I$; this family depends only on the reference ellipse, interval, and anchor. The main linear result classifies all real $L^2$ displacements satisfying the constant rational orbit-sum equations throughout $I$ as infinitesimal ellipse deformations, and establishes their analyticity and rational continuation in the complexified boundary parameter. The proof combines analytic continuation and elimination of monodromy with quantitative caustic estimates, finite detection, and Fourier interpolation.

papers.title: A curved three-dimensional simplex Hilbert transform
papers.authors: Polona Durcik, Marco Fraccaroli, Joris Roos
papers.abstract: We prove Lebesgue space estimates for a curved three-dimensional simplex Hilbert transform associated with the moment curve $t \mapsto (t,t^2,t^3)$. The analysis relies on smoothing inequalities for curved multilinear averages and on estimates for a three-dimensional anisotropic variant of the twisted paraproduct. The result has been formally verified in Lean 4.

papers.title: $\frac{1}{2}$ derivations and biderivations of 3-dimensional nilpotent Lie-Yamaguti algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations and their corresponding local and 2-local analogues on three-dimensional nilpotent Lie--Yamaguti algebras over a field $\mathbb{F}$ of characteristic zero. Utilizing the established classification of these algebras, we explicitly determine their structures of $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations and biderivations. Furthermore, we characterize the matrix representations of their local $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations. Our findings demonstrate that, for the non-abelian algebras under consideration, the space of local $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations is strictly larger than that of ordinary $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations. In addition, we construct examples of 2-local $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations that fail to be global $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations. Finally, a complete characterization of the biderivations for these algebras is provided.

papers.title: Operators commuting with $L^\infty$]{Operators commuting with $L^\infty$ on K\"othe--Bochner spaces
papers.authors: Hulya Duru, Serkan Ilter, Arkady Kitover, Mehmet Orhon
papers.abstract: Let $E(X)$ be a K\"othe--Bochner space of functions on a $\sigma$-finite measure space with values in a Banach space $X$. We study bounded operators on $E(X)$ that commute with the operators of multiplication by functions from $L^\infty$. If $X$ is separable, every such operator acts pointwise by an essentially bounded $L(X)$-valued function. For a nonseparable $X$, a lifting of $L^\infty$ provides a representation by $L(X,X^{\star\star})$-valued functions, and by $L(X)$-valued functions if $X$ is complemented in $X^{\star\star}$, with the sharp norm bound if $X$ is a dual space. As an application, we show that if the transformation is aperiodic, then the spectral projections of invertible weighted composition operators with operator-valued weights are operators of multiplication by $L(X)$-valued functions whenever $X$ is separable or complemented in $X^{\star\star}$, and that, if moreover the measure is ergodic and $\dim X = m < \infty$, the spectrum of such an operator has at most $m$ connected components. Finally, for $L^p(\mu;X)$, $1 \leq p < \infty$, an aperiodic nonsingular transformation and a weight that is measurable in the operator norm, we prove that the spectral projections are operators of multiplication by projection-valued functions for an arbitrary Banach space $X$, for instance for $X = c_0(\Gamma)$ with $\Gamma$ uncountable. The proof uses an inverse-closedness result for the algebra generated by norm-measurable multipliers and the composition operator.

papers.title: Invariant and Super-median Functions for Perturbed Heat Kernels
papers.abstract: We study super-median and invariant functions for positive and negative Schr\"odinger perturbations of non-negative kernels. For positive perturbations, combining Dynkin's formula for the original kernel with Duhamel's formula for the perturbation, we derive perturbed Dynkin-type identities and give integrability conditions ensuring invariance. When the perturbed kernel is given by the perturbation series, we obtain a sufficient condition for a function to be super-median without additional integrability assumptions. We also decompose every finite non-negative solution of Duhamel's equation into the perturbation series and a non-negative solution of the corresponding homogeneous equation. For negative perturbations, we obtain analogous identities under an explicit finiteness condition. We also construct functions satisfying Dynkin's formula using zero-resolvents and compensated kernels. Examples involving Gaussian, fractional, and Bessel kernels illustrate the invariance criteria and the role of non-uniqueness in Duhamel's equation.

papers.title: Symplectophagy
papers.authors: Adi Dickstein, Yaniv Ganor, Frol Zapolsky
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of a symplectophagy, which is a symplectic isotopy satisfying conditions reminiscent of the symplectic camel. We present new symplectic rigidity results which take the form of obstructions to the existence of symplectophagies in certain situations. The main tool is the relative symplectic cohomology recently introduced by Varolgunes, as well as its extension to pairs, due to the authors and L. Polterovich, for which we establish an invariance property, which is the chief technical novelty of the present paper. An important role is also played by the recent calculations of relative symplectic cohomology in complex projective spaces due to Dickstein-Ganor.

papers.title: Adaptive First-Order Methods with Composite Gradient Error
papers.authors: Artem Vasin, Alexander Tyurin, Alexander Gasnikov
papers.abstract: We study first-order optimization with inexact gradients whose errors combine a component proportional to the true gradient norm and a uniformly bounded absolute component. We develop an adaptive gradient descent scheme that selects estimates of the smoothness constant and both error parameters through a computable backtracking condition using exact function values. Its analysis yields convergence for smooth objectives and functions satisfying Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition. For strongly convex objectives, we propose a composite-error intermediate gradient method, that adapts to unknown smoothness while using known error bounds and a strong convexity parameter $\mu$. With fixed smoothness $L$, acceleration is retained when $\alpha=\mathcal{O}\left(\left(\mu / L \right)^{1/4}\right)$, larger admissible errors yield intermediate rates. Throughout the range $0 \leqslant \alpha \leqslant 1/3$, the absolute error bound $\delta$ contributes at most $\mathcal{O} \left(\delta^2/\mu \right)$ to the objective residual, without additional amplification by the condition number.

papers.title: On the classification of threefold flops
papers.abstract: We show that possibly singular threefold flopping contractions are completely classified by their associated derived contraction algebras, considered up to derived Morita equivalence; in contrast to the smooth case the extra derived structure is necessary in general. This extends previous work of the author on simple flops, and follows from a more general theorem about isolated hypersurface singularities. The key new input is to show that derived localisation at a Hochschild class is Morita invariant; this result raises some interesting questions related to the classification of recollements. We also show that derived contraction algebras admit a deformation-theoretic interpretation in families in a general setting that encompasses threefold flops, flips, and divisor-to-curve contractions.

papers.title: Random-subspace Ellipsoidal Trust-region Methods for Derivative-free Optimization
papers.abstract: Random-subspace model-based methods offer a promising approach to solving derivative-free optimization (DFO) problems in high dimensions. However, the usual ratio of actual to predicted reduction assesses model agreement at the trial point without directly measuring subspace quality. An accurate prediction in a poorly aligned subspace may therefore trigger trust-region expansion in all directions. We introduce Random-subspace Ellipsoidal TRust-region Optimization (RETRO), a framework for unconstrained DFO using ellipsoidal trust regions. Its trust-region updates combine global size changes with additional expansion or contraction within the sampled subspace, reflecting where the trial step was computed. We define an ellipsoidal subspace alignment measure that accounts for both the subspace and trust-region shape, and analyze Haar-uniform sampling and metric-guided sampling based on the current shape matrix. We establish almost-sure first-order liminf convergence and an $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-2})$ bound on the expected number of iterations required to reach an iterate with gradient norm at most $\epsilon$. Numerical experiments on projected low-rank problems in dimension $1000$ show that using ellipsoidal shape information in subspace selection can reduce function evaluation costs relative to ball-based QARSTA, with the most pronounced improvements occurring when the solver subspace dimension matches the projection rank.

papers.title: A Partial Duty Formulation for Crew Scheduling
papers.authors: Twan Dollevoet, Bart van Rossum, Remy Spliet
papers.abstract: We consider a crew scheduling problem with a break, working time, and duty length constraint. It is common to solve crew scheduling problems with a diving heuristic, using column generation to solve the LP relaxation of a set partitioning formulation where variables correspond with duties. We prove that computing the LP bound of this formulation is weakly NP-hard, and propose an alternative formulation based on partial duties, whose LP bound can be computed in polynomial time. We prove the same complexity results for the corresponding pricing problems. However, the partial duty formulation has a weaker LP bound. To overcome this issue, we introduce compatibility cuts which completely recover the loss in LP bound. While separation can be done efficiently, we prove that the corresponding pricing problem after separation is weakly NP-hard. Therefore, we also introduce two relaxed versions of the compatibility cuts. We demonstrate computational benefits by providing numerical experiments with a diving heuristic based on the partial duty formulation, in a case study on the metro network of the Rotterdam area, the Netherlands.

papers.title: A characterization of generalized derivations and biderivations on some simple algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we characterize the generalized derivations and biderivations of the simple seven-dimensional anticommutative algebra \(D\) and the seven-dimensional central simple commutative algebra \(C\). Furthermore, we prove that any local generalized derivation of these algebras is inherently a generalized derivation.

papers.title: Index-one capillary minimal hypersurfaces in \(\mathbb R^n_+\)
papers.abstract: We classify complete, two-sided, properly embedded capillary minimal surfaces with nonempty boundary and Morse index one in \(\mathbb R^3_+\). More precisely, if the boundary is compact, these surfaces are catenoid truncations; if the boundary is noncompact, they are capillary hairpin surfaces. The classification extends to higher dimensions under extrinsic Euclidean volume growth and Wang--Zhang's dimension and angle conditions.

papers.title: Calder\'on Commutators on Quantum Euclidean Spaces and Quantum Tori
papers.abstract:
In the classical setting, Calder\'on's first commutator theorem states that Lipschitz regularity of the symbol characterizes the $L_2$-boundedness of the first commutators. We show that the formally analogous assertion fails on every quantum Euclidean space $\R^d_\theta$ with $\theta\neq 0$. The same simultaneous failure occurs on $\T_\theta^d$ whenever $\theta$ has an irrational entry. For rational $\theta$, we obtain the optimal logarithmic bound for the corresponding Calder\'on first commutator. We also discuss the connection between Calder\'on's first commutator and the $T1$ theorem, and construct an operator-valued counterexample to Calder\'on's first commutator theorem, which shows that there is no direct analogue of the classical $T1$ theorem in the operator-valued setting.
  The counterexamples and the optimality argument rely on the construction of sequences of matrices $\mathsf D_n$ and $\mathsf A_n$ such that $\|[\mathsf D_n,\mathsf A_n]\|$ is uniformly bounded, whereas $\|[|\mathsf D_n|,\mathsf A_n]\|$ tends to infinity. This phenomenon reflects the failure of the absolute value function to be operator Lipschitz with respect to the operator norm. The logarithmic estimate, on the other hand, is obtained by combining matrix-valued $T1$ theory with a transference argument.

papers.title: Entropy-Regularized Finite-State Mean Field Control: Regularity and Stability
papers.abstract: We study infinite-horizon discounted mean field control of finite-state continuous-time Markov chains with unbounded transition rates and a relative-entropy rate penalty. Under mild assumptions, the value function is the unique bounded viscosity solution of the stationary Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation on the closed probability simplex. Joint convexity of a quadratically corrected flux Lagrangian and smoothness of the data yield global semiconvexity, intrinsic $\mathcal{C}^{1,1}$ regularity, and optimal Gibbs feedback. For positive symmetric reference rates, an entropy-plus-value free energy gives global exponential convergence under a quantitative curvature condition. We also establish inverse-temperature limits for values and, under parameter-uniform hypotheses, for feedbacks and closed-loop trajectories. With population-independent reference rates and a potential state-cost structure, optimal planner trajectories induce discounted finite-state mean field game equilibria. As an application, size-dependent market-making quotes with exponential demand admit an exact revenue-to-entropy reformulation; a convex inventory-crowding potential connects optimal quoting to stabilization of the inventory distribution.

papers.title: Alp\"oge's counterexample to the JC, Economic Stabilization, and Zhao's Vanishing Conjecture
papers.abstract: In this paper, we apply stabilization techniques which are economic in the number of added dimensions to a slightly tweaked version of Alp\"oge's counterexample to JC(3) and JC(3,7). The first idea which lead to more economic stabilization is to bypass the degree 3 reduction of Bass, Connell and Wright in the construction of a counterexample to HJC(n). We construct counterexamples to HJC(15), VC(28), and HVC(30). On the other hand, we will perform degree 3 reduction after all to obtain counterexamples of low degree. We construct counterexamples to JC(12,3), HJC(18,3), VC(34,4), and HVC(36,4). As an encore, we construct a cubic-linear counterexample to the Jacobian Conjecture in dimension 90. All presented counterexamples to the Jacobian Conjecture (Vanishing Conjecture) are over the (Gaussian) integers.

papers.title: Query-Dependent Reading for Quantized Inner-Product Estimation: A Minimax Separation
papers.authors: Krishnakumar Balasubramanian, Siddharth Bhandari, Shiva Prasad Kasiviswanathan
papers.abstract:
We study quantization for inner-product estimation when storage and reading have separate budgets. In the static bit-probe model [Yao, 1981], an encoder stores $w$ bits about $x$ before seeing a query $y$, and a reader probes at most $r<w$ bits to estimate $x^\top y$. Both vectors lie in the $d$-dimensional Euclidean unit ball. Protocols may be randomized, and computation is unrestricted. Performance is measured by $d$ times the worst-case mean-squared error over $x,y$, averaged over protocol randomness.
  First, we show that query-independent reading cannot benefit from extra storage. Any such reader is equivalent to fully reading an $r$-bit message, even when later reads depend on previously returned bits. At fixed positive rates $W=w/d$ and $R=r/d$, the normalized minimax error converges to $1/(4^R-1)$, independent of $W$. The upper bound was already known [Ordentlich and Polyanskiy, 2025]. We prove the matching lower bound for arbitrary scalar decoders, extending the result for unbiased compressors [Safaryan et al., 2020].
  Then, we show that query-dependent reading makes extra storage useful. We construct a two-batch protocol using Gaussian projections and random thresholds, with asymptotic normalized error at most $(\pi+o(1))/[4R\log(W/R)]$ as $W/R\to\infty$. At fixed $R$, this error vanishes as storage grows, giving an unbounded advantage over query-independent reading. We also prove a finite-dimensional lower bound for arbitrary encoders, decoders, and fully branching readers. In the doubly sparse regime $W/R\to\infty$ and $R\log(W/R)\to0$, it gives normalized error at least $(1-o(1))/[2R\log(W/R)]$. Thus, our protocol is optimal within a factor of $\pi/2$ in the leading constant.

papers.title: All totally real abelian number fields of class number one are Euclidean
papers.abstract: It is a famous result of Narkiewicz that there are at most two real quadratic and at most one totally real cubic Galois extensions $K/\mathbb Q$, whose ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$ is a unique factorization domain (UFD), but not Euclidean. As predicted by another famous result due to Weinberger, these exceptions should in fact not exist, as their existence would contradict a generalized version of the Riemann hypothesis. Building on recent spectacular progress on the Quasi-Riemann hypothesis for Hecke characters, in this short note we close the above final gap provided by Narkiewicz's result, and show, more generally, that the ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$ of any totally real abelian number field $K$ is a UFD, if and only if it is Euclidean.

papers.title: Opposed Exponent Profiles and Real Interpolation of Measurable Subspaces
papers.abstract: We study real interpolation of the $G$-measurable subspaces $Y_j$ of variable Lebesgue spaces $L^{p_j(\cdot)}$. For a family of continuous exponent pairs that vary in opposite directions on the atoms of $G$, we prove that $K$-closedness is equivalent to a uniform logarithmic bound on the oscillation of the exponents. The same bound characterizes the existence of a common bounded projection and interpolation equality at a single interior parameter. If it fails, then for each $0<\theta<1$ there is one function belonging to all ambient interpolation spaces $(X_0,X_1)_{\theta,q}$, $0<q\leq\infty$, and to none of the corresponding spaces $(Y_0,Y_1)_{\theta,q}$. Each endpoint subspace still admits a bounded positive projection. The exponents can be chosen arbitrarily close to prescribed constants $1<a<b<\infty$, with constant sum and smoothness away from zero. We also give a finite-profile criterion in terms of the endpoint maxima, compute the associated $K$-functional loss, and obtain a counterexample for adapted sequence spaces.

papers.title: An explicit section of the Laudenbach-type exact sequence of the big mapping class group of $M_\Gamma$
papers.abstract: Given a locally finite graph $\Gamma$, Udall proved that the mapping class group of the doubled handlebody associated to $\Gamma$ is an extension of the mapping class group of $\Gamma$ by a possibly infinite direct product of $\mathbb{Z}_2$, and that this extension splits. We give a formula for Udall's section restricted to the pure mapping class group and, when $\Gamma$ has finitely many ends, on the whole mapping class group.

papers.title: Local Converse Theorems for $k$-Middle Supercuspidal Representations of $p$-adic $\text{GL}(kn)$
papers.authors: Moshe Adrian, Michael Horzepa, David C. Luo
papers.abstract: Let $\text{F}$ be a non-archimedean local field of characteristic zero with residual characteristic $p$. In this paper, we study local converse theorems for $k$-middle supercuspidal representations of $\text{GL}(kn, \text{F})$ via explicit computations of twisted gamma factors on the Galois side, under the assumptions $p \nmid kn$ and $q_{\text{F}}>(k-1)^2$. Our results provide further evidence for a conjecture of the third-named author and Stevens on depth bounds for the twisting representations in the local converse theorem. For odd $k \ge 3$, we obtain infinitely many families of supercuspidal representations for which the bound $\left\lfloor \frac{kn}{2} \right\rfloor$ in the local converse theorem is not sharp.

papers.title: The pattern of consistency strength for membership in a computably enumerable set
papers.abstract: Every computable preorder relation on the natural numbers is the order of consistency strength for the membership assertions "$n\in A$" in some computably enumerable set $A$. Moreover, for every computably enumerable list of theories $T_0,T_1,T_2,\ldots$, each extending PA, there is a computably enumerable set $A$ such that each $T_n$ is equiconsistent over PA with the membership assertion $n\in A$. And similarly for both results when using instead the nonmembership assertions $n\notin A$.

papers.title: Stein fillable contact structures with half Giroux torsion
papers.abstract: We show that there exist Stein fillable contact 3-manifolds which contain a separating half Giroux torsion layer. Our examples are on Seifert fibred spaces over the sphere.

papers.title: Hodge-Carleman estimates and global attractors for heterogeneous elastic waves with localized damping on Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: We study the long-time dynamics of the semilinear Lam\'e system of isotropic elasticity on a compact Riemannian manifold with boundary, for a heterogeneous medium whose density and Lam\'e moduli vary in space, under a frictional dissipation which acts only on an open set $\omega$. The elastic operator is the divergence of the Hooke stress tensor, and the starting point is a structural identity which shows that the dilatation and the vorticity of the displacement satisfy wave equations with the pressure and the shear speeds, respectively, coupled to the displacement only through first-order terms. A single weight function, free of critical points and strictly convex with respect to the two ray metrics of the medium, then serves for the displacement, its dilatation and its vorticity alike, and this Hodge structure yields Carleman estimates for the Lam\'e operator with variable coefficients at two energy levels, provided that $\omega$ contains a neighbourhood of the boundary and that such a weight exists on the undamped region. The hypothesis is fulfilled on every compact manifold with boundary by damping regions of arbitrarily small volume. From these estimates we derive unique continuation for elastic waves with bounded, merely measurable, time-dependent potentials and an internal observability inequality, which in turn yield, for subcritical restoring forces in dimension three, a compact global attractor which coincides with the unstable manifold of the equilibria, has finite fractal dimension and is bounded in $(H^2\cap H^1_0)\times H^1_0$, together with a generalized exponential attractor.

papers.title: Metric preservation under approximate algebraic laws
papers.abstract: We investigate which metric information can be retained when an initial metric space is realized in a complete algebra satisfying quantitative laws. Using free metric realizations, we express preservation of designated distances as constraints on the permitted errors. In a fixed weighted-path presentation, the associated feasible error budgets form a closed, convex, upward-closed region with finite-path certificates of failure, and free term distances depend continuously on the budgets. For an idempotent binary operation with positive coordinate weights $a+b=1$, we establish sharp associativity-defect bounds and an exact formula for the generator distances in the free realization with associativity tolerance $\alpha$: $\min\{d_X(x,y),\alpha/(ab)\}$. This yields explicit injectivity and isometry thresholds. We also give a necessary diameter bound when both idempotence and associativity are approximate, and a countably presented example whose free distance is continuous but not Lipschitz at zero.

papers.title: Sharp Weighted Sobolev Trace Inequalities on Convex Cones and Rigidity of Extremals
papers.authors: Jo\~ao Marcos do \'O, Lucas de Melo Pontes e Silva
papers.abstract: We study critical weighted Sobolev trace inequalities on convex cones endowed with positively homogeneous weights. Using mass transportation, we first establish the continuity of the critical trace embedding under general homogeneity and concavity assumptions on the weight. We then identify a compatibility condition between the weight, the cone, and a distinguished direction that makes the transport argument sharp. In this regime, we determine the optimal constant and prove the existence of extremals. Finally, we obtain a complete classification of all nontrivial extremals modulo translation in the lineality space.

papers.title: Local well-posedness of the two-dimensional Incompressible Schr\"odinger flow
papers.abstract: We consider the incompressible Schr\"odinger flow (ISF), an efficient model for simulating incompressible inviscid fluids introduced by Chern et al. \cite{C17,CKPSW16}, on a bounded, simply connected two-dimensional domain. After transforming it into the director formulation, the equation becomes the Schr\"odinger map (or the Landau--Lifshitz equation) transported by a velocity field generated from the director itself via Biot--Savart law. We show that the director formulation has a unique local-in-time strong solution. Then, we lift the solution to the director formulation to the spinor, and conclude that it is indeed a unique solution to the ISF. This result is a first rigorous analysis on ISF, a widely used computational model.

papers.title: Weighted homogeneous surface singularities admitting rational homology disk smoothings
papers.abstract: We study rational homology disk smoothings through canonical-cover representations and specialization of reflexive canonical powers, and recover the known dual graph and analytic classification. The geometric-genus representation of the canonical covering group, together with its complex conjugate, is a direct summand of the reduced regular representation. Specialization forces the canonical Riemann--Roch corrections to vanish; explicit formulas give equations for the Seifert invariants. For three arms and central weight two, these equations, the character restrictions, and the numerical identities determine the Seifert data without assuming the existence of a smoothing. Projective compactifications treat the remaining cases, and elliptic pencils explain the four-arm attachment points and the parameter independence of their cross ratios. We construct strong $\mathbb{Q}$-Gorenstein smoothings for all listed analytic structures by deforming canonical-cover equations and lifting generators of the full first syzygy module. The numerical Milnor formula gives rational homology disk fibers.

papers.title: Every commutative perfect ring is a quotient of an almost perfect domain
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that every nonzero commutative perfect ring is a quotient of a one-dimensional semilocal almost perfect domain of characteristic zero. The domain can be chosen to have as many maximal ideals as the given ring has local factors. The construction uses coefficient discrete valuation rings, triangular presentations of purely inseparable residue extensions, and approximation for finitely many independent rank-one valuations. Independent error variables keep the construction inside a field. A normal-form argument shows that the divided elements used to get perfect principal quotients do not kill any further good monomial. In positive residue characteristic, the choice $a=2c+1$ with $c\ge n$ protects the nonzero powers of $p$ in a target ring of characteristic $p^n$. We also give local and mixed-characteristic consequences, and examples with non-nilpotent radicals.

papers.title: Stable Ergodicity for Expanding on Average Partially Hyperbolic Diffeomorphisms with Two-Dimensional Center
papers.abstract:
We study a property called expansion on average (EA) defined for any partially hyperbolic diffeomorphism satisfying an unstable center bunching condition. Under a mild set of assumptions, we show that the EA property implies $C^2$-stable ergodicity with respect to volume. Our theorem applies to any conservative, $u$-center bunched, robustly dynamically coherent, partially hyperbolic $C^2$-diffeomorphism with two-dimensional center and one-dimensional unstable bundle, whose action on $E^c$ is close to conservative. We do not assume that the center leaves are compact or that the center foliation has a fibration structure. Our mechanism for ergodicity also does not use accessibility or the existence of a dominated splitting in $E^c$.
  The EA property is inspired by a condition with the same name defined for IID random dynamical systems on surfaces, and our proofs extend ideas from that setting. The EA property is systematically studied in very recent work of Carrasco-Obata-Saghin-Yang, where they obtain continuity of center Lyapunov exponents, strong positive recurrence, and existence of finitely many SRB measures. With input from our result, they obtain uniqueness of SRB measures for dissipative perturbations of certain EA diffeomorphisms.

papers.title: On the strong domination relation of order sequences for some group extensions
papers.abstract: Given a finite group $G$, its order sequence $os(G)$ is a sequence formed of the element orders of $G$ written in non-decreasing order. In [Electron. J. Combin. 32 (2025), no. 2, Paper No. 2.9], P. J. Cameron and H. K. Dey proved that if $G$ and $H$ are groups of coprime orders, $G$ is abelian and $K$ is any extension of $G$ by $H$, then there is a bijection $f$ from $G\times H$ to $K$ such that the order of $f(x)$ divides the order of $x$, for all $x\in G\times H$. In the same paper, the authors asked if the hypothesis ``$G$ is abelian" is necessary. We show that if this condition is dropped, the result does not hold in general.

papers.title: On the frequency function of periodic quasianalytic and non-quasianalytic functions
papers.abstract:
For a real-valued continuous periodic function $f$, let \[
  A_r f(x)=\frac{1}{2r}\int_{x-r}^{x+r}f(t)\,dt,\qquad A_0f(x)=f(x), \] and let $r_f(x)$ be the smallest radius at which $\sup_{r\geq 0}A_r f(x)$ is attained. We call $r_f$ the frequency function of $f$. Steinerberger proved that a two-valued condition involving both $r_f$ and $r_{-f}$ characterizes a single sinusoidal function, and asked if the same result holds under the assumption that $r_f$ has finite range (or even range with Lebesgue measure zero). In this paper, we prove that a stronger finite-valued condition for $r_f$ characterizes a sinusoidal function for the case when $f$ is periodic, smooth, and belongs to a quasianalytic Denjoy-Carleman class. However, we also show that the conjecture of Steinerberger is not true in general, since we can construct non-sinusoidal periodic smooth functions in non-quasianalytic Denjoy-Carleman classes such that their frequency functions have finite range.

papers.title: Large values of derivatives of quadratic Dirichlet $L$-functions
papers.authors: Zikang Dong, Ruihua Wang, Weijia Wang, Hao Zhang, Shengbo Zhao
papers.abstract: e study large values of fixed derivatives of quadratic Dirichlet $L$-functions on the real segment $1/2\leq\sigma\leq1$. Assuming GRH, we prove lower bounds in terms of GCD sums and finite Euler products. At the central point, every fixed derivative order is compared with the same square-free GCD sum. In the mesoscopic band $\sigma=1/2+A/\log_2X$, a renormalized resonator estimates contributions from both halves of the differentiated approximate functional equation. The resulting lower bound has a relative error. On a smaller boundary scale, a common finite product appears in both contributions to this lower bound. This allows us to locate the crossover between their derivative weights. The coarser exponential bounds have constant $1$ at the center and $\mathrm e^{-A}$ in the mesoscopic band. For fixed $1/2<\sigma<1$, the lower bound includes the full typical logarithmic weight of the resonating Euler product. Burgess truncation improves the exponential constant when a shorter cutoff allows a longer resonator. Near the $1$-line, our lower bounds involve Dickman constants on the $1/\log_2X$ scale. We also prove a uniform transition estimate outside a shrinking neighborhood of the central point. All results hold in the positive even subfamily of fundamental discriminants.

papers.title: Complete self-shrinkers with constant norm of the second fundamental form in \(\RR^4\)
papers.abstract: Let \(X:M^3\to\RR^4\) be a complete self-shrinker with constant squared norm \(S\) of the second fundamental form. We prove that \(S=0\) or \(S=1\), and that \(X(M)\) is isometric to a hyperplane or a standard product \(\SSS^k(\sqrt{k})\times\RR^{3-k}\), \(1\leq k\leq3\). This proves a conjecture proposed by Cheng and Wei for three-dimensional hypersurfaces.

papers.title: A Jost--Pais theorem for the intermediate long wave equation
papers.authors: Rowan Killip, Monica Vi\c{s}an, Yilun Wu
papers.abstract: For a one-dimensional Schr\"odinger operator, the transmission coefficient can be expressed as a Fredholm determinant. This fundamental discovery of Jost and Pais has recently proven very influential in the study of conserved quantities for the Korteweg--de Vries equation, whose Lax operator takes this form. In this paper, we obtain an analogue of this result for the intermediate long wave equation, where, startlingly, the transmission coefficient is given by a \emph{ratio} of Fredholm determinants. We then recover the original Jost--Pais result in the shallow-water limit and its analogue for the Benjamin--Ono equation as the infinite-depth limit.

papers.title: Equivalence of Restricted and Full Division
papers.abstract: We prove over $\mathrm{PA}^{-}$ that the restricted Euclidean division principle $\mathrm{pa17}^{-}$, which asserts division only for co-prime pairs, is equivalent to the full principle $\mathrm{pa17}$. The proof uses a transformation that preserves the quotient in division with remainder to reduce an arbitrary division problem to one for a co-prime pair. This answers Visser's Open Question 8.29 and shows that the restricted principle has the same strength as full Euclidean division over $\mathrm{PA}^{-}$.

papers.title: Bounded orbits on homogeneous spaces and bounded geodesics on locally symmetric spaces
papers.abstract:
We present a unified approach to proving the following two results:
  (i) Let $G$ be a Lie group, $\Gamma$ a lattice in $G$, $X=G/\Gamma$, and let $F$ be a one-parameter $\mathrm{Ad}$-diagonalizable subgroup of $G$. Then the set $$ \{x\in X:Fx\text{ is bounded in }X\} $$ is hyperplane absolute winning on $X$. This fully solves a conjecture [Conjecture 7.1]{AGK} of An-Guan-Kleinbock in 2015.
  (ii) Let $G$ be a connected semisimple Lie group with finite center and without compact factors, $K\leq G$ a maximal compact subgroup, $\Gamma\leq G$ a torsion-free lattice, and $M=K\backslash G/\Gamma$. Then for any $p\in M$, the set $$\{\xi\in S_pM:\gamma(p,\xi)\text{ is bounded in }M\}$$ is hyperplane absolute winning on $S_pM$, where $\gamma(p,\xi)$ denotes the geodesic ray through the base point $p$ in the direction $\xi$. This fully solves a conjecture [Conjecture 1.2]{GW26} of Guan-Wu in 2026.

papers.title: Eynard-Orantin Topological Recursion, Moduli-Space Virasoro Constraints, and Semisimple CohFTs
papers.abstract: We use Virasoro constraints to prove Eynard's intersection-number formula for Eynard-Orantin topological recursion with several simple ramification points. The key construction couples the higher Weil-Petersson partition functions associated with the individual ramification points through a quadratic differential operator determined by the Bergman kernel. We identify this operator with the quadratic part of Givental's quantized $R$-matrix, thereby obtaining a Virasoro-theoretic proof of the DOSS identification of topological recursion with Givental's formula for semisimple cohomological field theories. Furthermore, while the DOSS identification fixes the distinguished $y$-function, we keep the Bergman kernel/$R$-matrix fixed and allow $y$ to vary, showing that this amounts to shifting the evaluation point of the corresponding ancestor potential.

papers.title: Rank and Border Rank Additivity of Complex Tensors with a Hankel Summand
papers.abstract: We prove that the CP rank of a complex Hankel tensor of order $m\ge3$ is additive with that of every complex tensor of the same order. Together with the known equality of CP and symmetric ranks for complex Hankel tensors, this yields symmetric rank additivity whenever the other summand has equal CP and symmetric ranks. We also prove that ordinary and symmetric border ranks coincide and are additive on direct sums of complex Hankel tensors of any common order at least three. Their common value is the sum of the middle binary catalecticant ranks. For order three, we further prove border-rank additivity when the other summand has border rank at most three, or is symmetric with at most five essential variables.

papers.title: Pareto optimality under nondegeneracy at infinity
papers.authors: Liguo Jiao, Jae Hyoung Lee, Tien-Son Pham
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider a broad class of multiobjective optimization problems, which are defined in a simple and elegant manner by using only two basic notions of Newton polyhedra and nondegeneracy at infinity associated with given data. For each problem in the class, its several basic properties are studied; in particular, necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of (weakly/properly) efficient solutions as well as the H\"older-type global weak sharp minima are established.

papers.title: Convergence of Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models: A R\'{e}nyi Divergence Perspective
papers.authors: Wenliang Liu, Santiago Mazuelas, Guanding Yu, Renjie Liao, Lele Wang, Yuan Shen
papers.abstract: Denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) have emerged as a powerful framework for generative modeling by transforming standard Gaussian inputs into outputs that approximate a target distribution. While DDPMs have been proved to converge in total variation, KL divergence, and Wasserstein distance, these discrepancy measures share a fundamental limitation of being insensitive to distributional mismatch in low-probability regions. To address this, we adopt the stronger R\'enyi divergence as the discrepancy measure. Leveraging a Girsanov-type change-of-measure argument, we establish the first R\'enyi characterization of DDPMs to the best of our knowledge, showing that the total error decomposes into a mixing error, a discretization error, and a score estimation error. We assume the target distribution is sub-Gaussian and characterize the score error via the cumulant generating function, relaxing both the log-Sobolev-inequality and $L^\infty$-score-error conditions used in prior R\'enyi divergence analyses of inexact Langevin Monte Carlo, a score-based sampling algorithm closely related to DDPM. Our results also establish an iteration complexity for achieving $\epsilon$-accuracy in $\alpha$-R\'enyi divergence that is asymptotically proportional to $\alpha^3/\epsilon$. Finally, by extending our analysis, we establish the first R\'enyi divergence convergence guarantee for critically damped DDPMs, a kinetic variant governed by critically damped Langevin dynamics. Similar to existing characterizations of critically damped DDPMs, this result shares the structural scaling of standard DDPMs, differing by at most a logarithmic factor in the mixing error exponent, and supports the conjecture that critically damped DDPMs do not yield a theoretical improvement.

papers.title: Spectral Curves for Semisimple Conformal Frobenius Manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct connected spectral curves for semisimple conformal Frobenius manifolds with flat unit, using the periods of the second structure equation. Eynard-Orantin topological recursion on these curves reproduces the stable ancestor correlators of Givental-Teleman reconstruction. The spectral curves are defined on simply connected domains in the complex plane. We apply the construction to the quantum cohomology of $\mathbb P^n$ for $n\ge2$ at a point, obtaining explicit spectral curve data in terms of Hecke triangle groups and hypergeometric functions. Finally, for $\mathbb P^2$ and $\mathbb P^3$, we express the complete spectral curve data, including the bidifferentials, in classical modular and quasimodular forms.

papers.title: The section conjecture for generic pointed curves
papers.abstract: Let $k/\mathbb Q$ be finitely generated, let $g\geq3$ and $n\geq1$, and let $\mathcal M_{g,n/k}$ be the moduli stack of smooth proper genus-$g$ curves with $n$ distinct ordered markings. Put $K=k(\mathcal M_{g,n/k})$. We prove Grothendieck's section conjecture for the generic $n$-pointed genus-$g$ curve over $K$. Over both the moduli stack and its function field, the continuous sections of the arithmetic fundamental-group extension of the universal complete curve are, up to geometric conjugacy, exactly the $n$ tautological sections. The same classification holds for every geometrically pro-$\ell$ quotient, for every prime $\ell$. Together with Hain's determination of the rational points, these classifications give examples over fields finitely generated over $\mathbb Q$ with any prescribed positive number of rational points for which the full section conjecture holds. The proof builds on Hain's weighted-completion and nonabelian cohomology methods, with a hyperelliptic calculation providing the genus-three input. An integral normalizer lemma and moving-mark arguments pass from unipotent sections to geometrically pro-$\ell$ sections. Configuration spaces and Mochizuki's open Hom theorem yield the full profinite classification, and generic descent identifies the section classes over the moduli stack with those over $K$.

papers.title: The Sharp Generalized Bogomolov Inequality
papers.abstract: Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact Gauduchon and astheno-K\"ahler manifold. Using $L^p$-approximate critical Hermitian structures, we establish a sharp generalized Bogomolov inequality for holomorphic vector bundles on $X$, without any semistability assumption. We further characterize the equality case by studying the Hermitian-Yang-Mills flow. If equality holds, every Harder-Narasimhan-Seshadri filtration is by holomorphic subbundles, and its stable quotients admit projectively flat Hermitian metrics. If, in addition, the bundle is not $\omega$-semistable, then $X$ is projective.

papers.title: Pseudodifferential structure, rigidity, and sharpness for the Steklov problem on differential forms
papers.authors: Daguang Chen, Guotao Huang, Tingyu Liao
papers.abstract: We resolve four questions concerning Karpukhin's Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator on differential forms. First, for $0\leq p\leq n-2$, we prove that the operator is classical pseudodifferential of order one and compute its principal symbol, which is elliptic on the coclosed symbol space. This answers Open Question 7.19 in the survey of Colbois, Girouard, Gordon, and Sher [7]. Second, the symbol calculation yields a Weyl law with remainder $O(\tau^{n-2})$, resolving the smooth case of their Open Question 7.23 in [7]. Third, in the critical dimension $n=2p+2$, we show that conformal deformations of the Euclidean ball fixing the boundary metric preserve the full operator. Nonisometric metrics therefore retain all equalities in Karpukhin's initial equality range, disproving the isometry-rigidity assertion of Conjecture 2.12 in [19](the rigidity assertion of Conjecture 7.27 in [7]). Fourth, we establish the all-index sharpness asserted in Conjecture 2.13 in [19](the sharpness assertion of Conjecture 7.27 in [7]) in the class of smooth compact connected oriented Riemannian manifolds with boundary. For $p\geq1$, a shrinking-core construction inspired by the collapsing models of Ann\'e and Takahashi produces manifolds with fixed spherical boundary and explicit two-sided bounds for an initial eigenvalue cluster.

papers.title: Local Nevanlinna embedding for Hardy space of Dirichlet series below critical exponent
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate a problem posed by Saksman and Seip [ Contemp. Math., 2016] on whether functions in the Hardy space of Dirichlet series $\mathcal{H}^p$, \(0<p<2\), are locally in the Nevanlinna class of the critical half-plane \(\mathbb C_{1/2}\). We show that the local Nevanlinna embedding fails below critical exponent \(p=2\) by constructing $\mathcal{H}^p$-functions whose local logarithmic mass becomes unbounded as \(\real s\to 1/2^+\). This also clarifies the distinction between global Jessen-type logarithmic control and local boundary Nevanlinna behavior for Dirichlet series.

papers.title: Classification of twisted Yangians as coideal subalgebras of Yangians
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak g$ be a complex simple Lie algebra with an involution $\omega$. We classify the homogeneous right coideal subalgebras of the Yangian of $\mathfrak g$ whose classical limit is the enveloping algebra of the twisted current algebra, embedded in the standard way, without assuming any formula for the coaction. For nontrivial $\omega$, they form a family parametrized by a spectral parameter and an element of the center of the fixed-point subalgebra; for $\omega=\mathrm{id}$, only a spectral parameter occurs. All members of the family are isomorphic as graded algebras, through explicit isomorphisms. In particular, the twisted Yangians with a central correction introduced by Huang and Lu are coideal quantizations, and the $\imath$Yangian of quasi-split type $\mathsf A_{2n}$ is isomorphic to the traditional twisted Yangian studied by MacKay and by Belliard and Regelskis. The PBW property is proved uniformly from the classical affine Serre relations, without quantum defining relations. We also recover finite presentations in split and quasi-split types and verify the technical hypotheses of the quantum duality principle used by Lu, Wang, and Weekes.

papers.title: Thoughts on Quantum Events, Quantizing Gravity and von Neumann Algebras
papers.abstract: This short document presents no new results. It is a collection of related ideas that may lead to a way of quantizing gravity. To achieve this it may be relevant to use my recent new approach to quantum theory, which is based on quantum events. Given that most standard quantum texts do not define a mathematical object which corresponds to a physical event, the definition of a quantum event is motivated and discussed in detail. This in turn leads to the idea that the mathematical object that contains enough quantum events for describing a quantum system is a von Neumann algebra. The next idea is that the kinematics of special relativity (as embodied in flat Minkowski space) should be quantized as a first step in the program of the quantization of general relativity, that is, quantizing Einstein's equation. It must be emphasized that the events of special relativity are viewed as part of the kinematics, rather than of the dynamics of that theory. The same holds for general relativity. Similarly, I am viewing quantum events as part of the kinematics of quantum theory, even though some find this to be counterintuitive. An Appendix shows how ``collapse'' is easily understood in this new approach to quantum theory.

papers.title: The locally quaternion group is a countable $B$-group
papers.abstract: A group $G$ is a $B$-group if every primitive permutation group containing a regular subgroup isomorphic to $G$ is doubly transitive. We prove that the locally quaternion group $\mathrm{Dic}(C_{2^\infty},c)$, the extension of the Pr\"ufer $2$-group by an element squaring to its involution and inverting it, is a $B$-group. This gives an example of a countably infinite $B$-group. This answers Problem 13.30 of the Kourovka Notebook. The proof analyses the automorphism group of an orbital Cayley graph through the central involution. In the main case two half-flip automorphisms generate, with their conjugates, an elementary abelian normal subgroup whose orbits form a nontrivial block system; in the remaining case, where the pointwise stabilizers of the two cosets of the Pr\"ufer group have order two, the conjugates of the central translation generate an elementary abelian normal subgroup, which would be regular if the automorphism group were primitive; an affine lemma for the Pr\"ufer group excludes this. The proof does not depend on computer verification: its two finite case analyses are written out in full, and programs that re-check them are provided as ancillary files.

papers.title: Integrable building blocks for symplectic neural networks: learned-type layers, fiber-preserving layers, and what a single layer can do
papers.abstract: Exactly symplectic neural networks are built almost exclusively from shear maps and gain expressivity only through depth. We ask what else a single explicit symplectic layer can be. Observing that every layer in use is the exact flow of a Hamiltonian that is a function of commuting integrals, we obtain three families of layers: a learned-type layer, in which every conjugate pair is rotated, squeezed or sheared by a state-dependent amount and the type is found by training; moving-plane shears, residual symplectic maps outside the known ridge-function class; and fiber-preserving layers, which combine an unconstrained point transformation with a fiber translation at the cost of one linear solve. We characterize residual symplectic layers $x \mapsto x + J\nabla H(x)$: in one degree of freedom they are exactly the shears along a line, while from two degrees of freedom on a strictly larger class exists. Conjugating a learned-type layer by a symplectic network yields an exact one-parameter group with an exactly conserved learned Hamiltonian. In experiments on sixteen systems with one to forty degrees of freedom, against SympNets, H\'enonNets and learned-plane shear networks, layers built on nonlinear integrals are far more accurate when the Hamiltonian contains functions of those integrals. On nonlinear Schr\"odinger lattices with six to forty sites, twist layers alternating with linear symplectic maps are over a hundred times more accurate than every shear-based network, and with an on-site potential of learned form three to four orders of magnitude more accurate. On chains of Tao oscillators with the step size as an input, stretch layers are 45 to 70 times more accurate than learned-plane shears and recover the Hamiltonian to 1%. On generic non-separable systems, fiber layers improve on learned-plane shears by at most a factor of two, and widening the networks does not help any architecture.

papers.title: Moreau-Yosida Penalization of McKean-Vlasov Dynamics: Full-Flux Limits and Boundary Reaction Measures
papers.authors: Geuntaek Seo, Beomjun Choi, Yeoneung Kim
papers.abstract: We study McKean-Vlasov Fokker-Planck dynamics on a compact convex set $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ through the whole-space Moreau-Yosida penalization $U_\lambda=\operatorname{dist}(\cdot,K)^2/(2\lambda)$, keeping the external and interaction potentials fixed. At finite times, the penalized densities converge to the unique variational solution of the reflected no-flux equation, strongly in space-time $L^2$ on $K$ and in whole-space $L^1$, and narrowly, uniformly in time. We prove that the singular penalty-force measures converge weakly-$*$ to the purely normal boundary reaction $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho)n\,\mathcal{H}^{d-1}|_{\partial K}\,\mathrm{d}t$. This measure cancels exactly the surface singularity in the distributional gradient of the zero-extended density, explaining the emergent no-flux condition at the flux level. At equilibrium, we establish sharp $\sqrt\lambda$ rates in $L^1$ and Wasserstein distances for kernel-free Gibbs states, and in $L^1$ and quadratic Wasserstein distance for interacting fixed points under Dobrushin smallness or positive semidefiniteness, including maximum mean discrepancy interactions. The proof combines a tilted Gaussian supersolution, nonautonomous weighted energy estimates, and normal factorization with a Green-formula identification. We also identify the limit with a nonlinear reflecting diffusion, obtain path-space convergence and $\lambda$-uniform propagation of chaos through monotone synchronous coupling, and derive all-time Gibbs domination in the reversible case. Numerical experiments illustrate the boundary reaction and stationary scalings on a constrained maximum mean discrepancy flow.

papers.title: Lambda number of the reduced power graph of finite groups
papers.authors: Siddharth Malviy, Keerttiranjan Sahoo, Vipul Kakkar
papers.abstract: The reduced power graph $\Gamma_{RP}(G)$ of a group $G$ is a simple graph with vertex set $G$, where two distinct vertices $u$ and $v$ are adjacent if and only if $\langle u \rangle \subset \langle v \rangle$ or $\langle v \rangle \subset \langle u \rangle$. An $L(2,1)$-labeling of a graph $\Gamma$ is a mapping from the vertex set of $\Gamma$ to the set of non-negative integers such that the labels of adjacent vertices differ by at least $2$ and the labels of vertices at distance two are distinct. The lambda number of $\Gamma$, denoted by $\lambda(\Gamma)$, is defined as the minimum possible span of labels among all $L(2,1)$-labelings of $\Gamma$. In this paper, we establish upper and lower bounds for $\lambda(\Gamma_{RP}(G))$ and characterize the conditions under which these bounds are achieved. As an application, we determine the exact value of $\lambda(\Gamma_{RP}(G))$ for certain classes of finite groups.

papers.title: A characterization of finite modular 2-groups via magnitude homology
papers.abstract: Finite quasihamiltonian groups - that is, finite groups in which every pair of subgroups commutes - admit several characterizations. In this work, after introducing the notion of sectional contractibility graph, we provide a new characterization in terms of (a suitable subgroup of) magnitude homology. Our approach especially focuses on the subgroup lattices of finite groups and on the related notion of modularity. We present a detailed study for finite 2-groups, and, in particular, in the case of extraspecial 2-groups and Pauli groups. These groups, of interest because of their diverse applications in both mathematics and physics, already describe the wealth of information that one can obtain in restricting the study to the case of 2-groups.

papers.title: Saddle Codazzi tensor on spheres and hemisphere rigidity
papers.authors: Jian Ge, Mijia Lai, Yuntian Zhu
papers.abstract:
Let $(M^n,g)$, $n\geq 3$, be a compact connected Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary. We ask whether $M$ must be isometric to the standard hemisphere if $\sec_g\geq 1$, $\partial M $ is isometric to the standard unit sphere, and its second fundamental form is Codazzi.
  Our approach centers on saddle Codazzi tensors on round spheres, where the saddle condition requires the restriction to every tangent two-plane to have nonpositive determinant. By analyzing the associated support maps, we prove that every smooth saddle Codazzi tensor on $\mathbb S^m$ vanishes identically for $m\geq 3$. Together with Panina's examples on $\mathbb S^2$, this shows that, among unit spheres of dimension at least two, nontrivial smooth saddle Codazzi tensors exist precisely in dimension two. The vanishing theorem yields an affirmative answer to the hemisphere rigidity question for $n\geq 4$.
  In dimension three, we realize the nontrivial saddle Codazzi tensors provided by Panina's construction, after scaling, as the second fundamental forms of smooth perturbations of the standard hemisphere, preserving the round boundary metric and the sectional curvature lower bound. This produces counterexamples to rigidity in dimension three. Nevertheless, under the same curvature and boundary assumptions, we prove the sharp inradius estimate $r_{\mathrm{in}}(M)\leq \pi/2$, with equality if and only if $M$ is isometric to the standard hemisphere.

papers.title: Schur-Positve Symmetric Functions from Products: Log-Majorization, Total-Positivity, and PSD Matrices
papers.abstract: For a polynomial $F(t) = 1 + a_1 t + a_2 t^2 +\dots + a_d t^d$ with coefficients in a $\mathbb{Q}$-algebra $\mathcal{R}$, we consider Schur-positivity of the symmetric function $\Omega_F(\mathbf{x}) = \prod_{i \geq 1} F(x_i)$. Using work of Lindstr\"om and Gessel--Viennot, we give sufficient conditions for Schur-positivity in terms of directed networks. In the case when $F(t)$ is the multivariate independence polynomial of the incomparability graph $inc(P)$ of a natural unit interval order, we apply these ideas to give a new proof of Schur-positivity of the chromatic symmetric function $X_{inc(P)}(\mathbf{x})$. Additionally, we prove Schur-positivity of certain sums of chromatic symmetric functions, refining recent work of Amdeberhan--Shareshian--Stanley. In the case when $\mathcal{R} = \mathbb{Q}[z_1,z_2,\dots,z_n]$, we prove necessary and sufficient conditions for Schur-positivity in terms of symmetric function evaluations. In particular, we show for $\mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v} \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^n$, $s_\lambda(\mathbf{u}) \geq s_\lambda(\mathbf{v})$ for all partitions $\lambda$ if and only if $m_\lambda(\mathbf{u}) \geq m_\lambda(\mathbf{v})$ for all partitions $\lambda$, and these inequalities are equivalent to $\mathbf{u}$ log-majorizing $\mathbf{v}$. Using representation theory of $GL(\mathbb{C}^n)$, we prove Schur-positivity of $\Omega_F(\mathbf{x})$ when $F(t) = \det(I + t\sum_{i = 1}^m z_i \mathbf{v}_i \mathbf{v}_i^*)$ for a collection of vectors $\mathbf{v}_1,\mathbf{v}_2,\dots, \mathbf{v}_m \in \mathbb{C}^n$. As an application for this result, we introduce the Kirchhoff symmetric function $K_G(\mathbf{x})$ of a loopless graph $G$ and show that it it always Schur-positive.

papers.title: Exponential loss of memory for random Lasota--Yorke convex maps with local average expansion
papers.abstract: We study i.i.d. random compositions of piecewise convex interval maps whose first branch is full. Uniform expansion is not required, and the maps may have contracting branches. Under a local average expansion condition at the origin, we prove both quenched and annealed exponential loss of memory for initial densities of bounded variation. The proof is based on a coupling argument. As applications, we obtain the quenched almost sure invariance principle and a rate of convergence in the quenched central limit theorem.

papers.title: Globally Optimal Estimation of Nested Logit Models
papers.abstract: Nested logit is widely used in operational demand models, yet jointly estimating its utility coefficients and nest dissimilarity parameters requires nonconvex optimization. Standard estimation routines offer no certificate of global optimality, leaving a gap between globally optimizing decisions under nested-logit demand and reliably estimating that demand model. We develop, to our knowledge, the first globally convergent optimization framework with an explicit global-accuracy guarantee for joint nested-logit estimation. Our central complexity result confines all exponential dependence to the number of free nest dissimilarity parameters: computation is polynomial in the numbers of observations, alternatives, and utility coefficients. Consequently, under the stated compact-domain and relaxation-error conditions, fixing the number of nests yields an additive polynomial-time approximation scheme (PTAS). The framework exploits an exact exponential-cone formulation for fixed dissimilarities and a spatial branch-and-bound algorithm that searches only over the free dissimilarities. Valid likelihood bounds provide an anytime certificate and finite termination at any prescribed additive average-log-likelihood tolerance. Across eight benchmark datasets and 240 estimation instances, the method certifies every reported solution and exposes inferior local estimates despite normal solver termination. These results establish a computational foundation for globally certified nested-logit estimation.

papers.title: A Self-Coupling Gaussian Extremal Inequality for Information-Constrained Optimal Transport with Applications to Rate-Distortion-Perception
papers.authors: Jiayang Zou, Jun Chen, Ayfer \"{O}zg\"{u}r, Jia Wang
papers.abstract: How much mutual information is needed to achieve a target correlation between two copies of a prescribed distribution? We prove a sharp Gaussian extremal inequality for this self-coupling problem: among distributions with a fixed mean and covariance, the Gaussian has the greatest minimum information cost for meeting a positive semidefinite cross-covariance target. The inequality is strict for non-Gaussian distributions when the target is positive definite. The proof uses a midpoint gluing construction. Two Ornstein--Uhlenbeck half-bridges, each started from the prescribed endpoint law, meet at a common intermediate distribution and are joined by conditional gluing. Changing the Gaussian reference then turns the resulting relative-entropy bound into the desired extremal inequality. As a first application, scaling one endpoint of the self-coupling establishes Gaussian extremality for rate-distortion-perception with unlimited common randomness, under quadratic distortion and squared Wasserstein-2 perception measures. We also establish an analogous result for finite common randomness, where the problem involves two mutual information constraints associated with an auxiliary random variable. In that setting, we retain an intermediate observation on one half-bridge and balance the two information budgets simultaneously using the Poincar\'{e}-Miranda theorem.

papers.title: Moser Regularization of the CR3BP for Symmetric Orbits: Bifurcation Networks of Lunar Orbits
papers.abstract: We develop a computational framework based on Moser regularization for the analysis of symmetric periodic orbits in the spatial Circular Restricted Three-Body Problem (CR3BP). The formulation enables the numerical continuation of periodic orbit families through collision with either primary, together with the computation of Floquet multipliers and stability indices entirely in regularized coordinates. We further provide a characterization and numerical detection scheme for symmetric periodic collision orbits. We apply this framework to the Earth-Moon CR3BP and uncover bifurcation networks connecting several classical lunar periodic orbit families. Higher-period vertical bifurcations of the planar $L_1$ Lyapunov family generate spatial bridges reconnecting different regions of the same family across its collision with the Earth, while corresponding bifurcations of the $L_2$ Lyapunov family form bridges to planar families associated with retrograde comet orbits. Furthermore, period-multiplying bifurcations of Near-Rectilinear Halo Orbit (NRHO) families produce a systematic network connecting to planar prograde and retrograde families. These bifurcation connections in the near-Moon dynamics retain the characteristic organization by covering multiplicities of the corresponding bifurcation network in the limiting Hill problem. Conley-Zehnder indices and related symplectic invariants complement the numerical continuation and provide a topological organization of the results.

papers.title: Proving the optimality of the product construction for the intersection--union problem
papers.authors: Fan Chang, Peter Frankl, Jian Wang
papers.abstract: Let $m(n,p,q)$ be the largest size of a family of subsets of $[n]$ whose members pairwise intersect in at least $p$ vertices and omit at least $q$ common vertices. We prove that a product on disjoint sets attains this maximum whenever $p,q\ge2$ and $n\ge2^{15}(p+q-2)^3$. Together with the second author's result for $p=1$ or $q=1$, this establishes Frankl's Intersection--Union Product Conjecture in a wide range.

papers.title: Probabilistic Powerdomains of Pointed FS-Domains are FS-Domains
papers.authors: Xiaoyong Xi, Chong Shen, Dongsheng Zhao
papers.abstract: The Jung-Tix problem concerns the compatibility of probabilistic powerdomains with Cartesian closed categories of domains. We prove that both the subprobability and probability valuation powerdomains of every pointed FS-domain are FS-domains.

papers.title: The 3-adic Steinberg block and a categorical 3-adic local Langlands correspondence for $\text{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_3)$
papers.abstract: We extend the work of Johansson-Newton-Wang-Erickson on a categorical $p$-adic Langlands correspondence over $\text{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$ to $p = 3$ by recontextualizing their construction in the Steinberg case. We produce a novel, more categorical method of analyzing the properties of this construction without requiring an explicit algebraic presentation. As input to this argument, we also perform some new analysis of the representation theory of the $3$-adic Steinberg block of $\text{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_3)$, obtaining results complementing those of Pa\v{s}k\={u}nas.

papers.title: Classification of Hom--Lie structures on finite-dimensional simple Lie algebras
papers.authors: Jiacheng Sun, Chi Zhang, Haoran Zhu
papers.abstract: We classify the Hom--Lie structures on finite-dimensional simple Lie algebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from \(2\) and \(3\). Except for the three-dimensional simple Lie algebra and the Zassenhaus algebras, every such structure is a scalar multiple of the identity. In the two exceptional cases, we determine the full Hom--Lie space: it has dimension six for the three-dimensional algebra, while for a Zassenhaus algebra it consists precisely of the multiplication operators arising from the corresponding divided-power algebra. This proves a conjecture of Makhlouf and Zusmanovich.

papers.title: Graded Structures of $v$-adic Carlitz Multiple Polylogarithms and $v$-adic Multiple Zeta Values
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study $v$-adic Carlitz multiple polylogarithms and $v$-adic multiple zeta values.
