For $N=2$, Alfaro and Xiao \cite{AlfaroXiao2023} studied the long-time behavior of solutions with compactly supported initial data by constructing precise super- and sub-solutions. For $N \geq 3$, the absence of a comparison principle for the entire system presents a major difficulty. Using a weighted entropy method, we prove that every bounded nonnegative traveling profile connecting nonzero equilibria is constant, without imposing any monotonicity assumption. For nontrivial compactly supported initial populations, we further show that the species with the strictly largest Fisher-KPP speed excludes all slower species and spreads at its scalar Fisher-KPP speed. Finally, we establish heat-type lower bounds for the slower species, revealing a bump phenomenon despite their uniform extinction.

papers.title: Commutators of a class of $\Psi$-bounded oscillation operators on abstract weighted Orlicz-Morrey spaces endowed with ball-basis and applications
papers.authors: Fate Shan, Wei Wang, Yuchen Li, Jiang Zhou
papers.abstract: In our previous work \cite{SZ2026}, we established a class of abstract Orlicz-Morrey spaces endowed with a ball-basis and introduced the notion of \(\Psi\)-bounded oscillation operators. The present paper further develops this theory by investigating sparse domination and weighted estimates for such operators and their commutators within the framework of abstract Orlicz-Morrey spaces endowed with a ball-basis. We obtain pointwise sparse domination results for the operators and establish their boundedness on weighted Orlicz-Morrey spaces. The hypotheses of these conclusions differ from those in the classical Orlicz-Morrey setting and do not rely on dyadic decompositions of Euclidean structure. Moreover, we study the duality of these spaces and prove that the dual of the associated block space is exactly the Orlicz-Morrey space under consideration.

papers.title: Arithmetic purity of strong approximation for complete intersections of large dimension
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that for a smooth complete intersection $X\subset \mathbb{P}^n$ of type $(d_1,\dots,d_c)$ over a number field $k$, there exists an effective bound $N_{\mathrm{AP}}(d_1,\dots,d_c)$ such that if $n\ge N_{\mathrm{AP}}(d_1,\dots,d_c)$, then $X$ satisfies arithmetic purity of strong approximation. We establish a connecting lemma that promotes weak approximation to strong approximation under a suitable connectivity hypothesis via rational curves over $k$. We construct the required connecting conics by combining the deformation theory of rational curves with results from the circle method.

papers.title: The Spherical Hadwiger Theorem
papers.abstract: We prove the spherical Hadwiger theorem in every dimension: for $n\geq1$, every continuous $\mathrm{SO}(n+1)$-invariant valuation on all closed spherical convex sets in the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^n$ is a unique linear combination of the spherical intrinsic volumes $V_0,\ldots,V_n$. The same classification holds on sets contained in an open hemisphere, with unique continuous invariant extension to the full domain. We first classify simple invariant valuations by an independent induction on dimension. Averaging a signed cone identity gives the spherical volume term; the remaining terms are signed coning transforms that vanish by the lower-dimensional simple classification. A second induction, together with extension to non-proper sets, gives the general classification. The cone--sphere correspondence yields, for $d\geq2$, the corresponding classification on all closed convex cones in $\mathbb{R}^d$, without normalization at the zero cone. In both settings, $\mathrm{SO}$-invariance implies $\mathrm{O}$-invariance.

papers.title: Recovering Laplacian Lattices from $L$-Functions of Graphs
papers.abstract: We introduce $L$-functions associated with characters of the Jacobian of a finite graph, as a graph-theoretic analogue of the $L$-functions arising from unramified coverings of algebraic curves. These $L$-functions are defined using the Riemann--Roch structure on the graph and extend Lorenzini's two-variable zeta function. We show that if two connected graphs without bridges have isomorphic Jacobians and their $L$-functions agree under the induced correspondence of characters, then their Laplacian lattices coincide. We also show that these $L$-functions satisfy a functional equation. Finally, we give examples showing that neither the Jacobian nor the Lorenzini zeta function alone determines the Laplacian lattice.

papers.title: Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures
papers.abstract: We study the geography of taut foliations on compact $3$-manifolds with toroidal boundary components. The central object of our work is the set of boundary multislopes realized by foliations transverse to a fixed flow on such a manifold. We prove that these sets exhibit remarkable structural properties (rationality, rigidity, and convexity) which motivate the name ziggurats. Our main tool, of independent interest, is a two-way correspondence between foliations and contact structures on $3$-manifolds with boundary: we generalize the Eliashberg-Thurston theorem, which produces pairs of positive and negative contact structures from foliations, and a construction of the first author, which builds foliations from such contact pairs. Using both directions of this correspondence, we bring contact-geometric methods to bear on the architecture of ziggurats.

papers.title: Effective Joint Equidistribution of Subspaces of Bounded Height in Rigid Adelic Spaces
papers.abstract: We prove an effective joint equidistribution theorem for $d$-dimensional $K$-subspaces, $1\le d<n$, of a fixed $n$-dimensional rigid adelic space over a number field $K$. The parameters are the height, the image in the archimedean Grassmannian, and the isometry classes of the subspace and quotient after each is rescaled to height $1$. For bounded Lipschitz test functions, the error term is power-saving with an explicit exponent. As an application, our theorem refines Thunder's asymptotic formula for subspaces of bounded height. We also obtain a power-saving asymptotic for subspaces containing $d$ linearly independent projective points of bounded height, with a leading constant expressed as a moment of the last successive minimum.

papers.title: Isodiametric-type upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues
papers.abstract: Let $n\geq 2$. We establish isodiametric-type upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues of bounded Lipschitz domains $\Omega$ in Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ and hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^n$. In Euclidean space, we prove \[ D(\Omega)\sigma_k(\Omega)\leq C(n)k, \] with optimal dependence on $k$. For domains in either $\mathbb{R}^n$ or $\mathbb{H}^n$, we establish \[ D(\Omega)\sigma_k(\Omega)\leq C(n)k^2\left(\frac{|\Omega|^{\frac{1}{n}}}{D(\Omega)}\right)^{\frac{n}{n-1}}. \] The exponent of the volume-diameter ratio is optimal in both settings, and with this exponent fixed, the quadratic dependence on $k$ is also optimal. Interpolating the preceding volume-diameter estimate with a volume-normalized Steklov bound, we further obtain \[ D(\Omega)\sigma_k(\Omega)\leq C(n)k^{1+\frac{1}{2n-1}} \] in hyperbolic space. These results answer Open Question 4.37 affirmatively and resolve the hyperbolic part of Open Question 4.35, both posed in [5].

papers.title: Reduced APN permutations and a disproof of the Galois-ring lifting conjecture
papers.abstract: We construct infinite families of reduced almost perfect nonlinear (APN) permutations of $\mathbb{F}_{2^m}$ that admit coefficientwise permutation lifts to $\mathrm{GR}(2^k,m)$ for every $k>1$. These families disprove Conjecture~2 of R\o njom and Sandrib (Cryptogr. Commun., 2026), even for reduced polynomial representatives. For every odd $m\ge5$ with $3\nmid m$, we obtain explicit seven-term polynomials over $\mathbb{F}_2$ with formal derivative identically one. We derive them from a complete criterion for the reduced representative of $A(x)^{2^s+1}$ to have no critical point in $\mathbb{F}_{2^m}$, where $A$ is an invertible linearized polynomial and $\gcd(s,m)=1$. We then apply the cube case to construct a second family of degree $2^{m-1}+2$, whose nonconstant derivatives avoid zero by an explicit trace identity. A fixed parameter in $\mathbb{F}_{32}$ gives this family in every dimension $m=5r$ with $r$ odd, including a degree-$18$ example over $\mathbb{F}_{32}$. Both constructions remain in Gold linear equivalence classes, so liftability of reduced representatives is not invariant under invertible $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear input changes. We obtain the lifting conclusions from the standard Galois-ring permutation criterion. We also verify a degree-$24$ example supplied by Zhang and Haobo, prove a trace-adjoint criterion for reduced quadratic functions, and interpret the derivative condition through ramification at rational points.

papers.title: Morita equivalent blocks with an endotrivial source that are not globally isotypic
papers.abstract: Let $(K,\mathcal{O},k)$ be a large enough $2$-modular system. We construct two nilpotent block algebras of finite groups which are isomorphic as $\mathcal{O}$-algebras and are Morita equivalent via a bimodule with an endotrivial source of $\mathcal{O}$-rank $3$, but which are not globally isotypic. Hence they are not $2$-permutation equivalent and not splendidly Rickard equivalent. These results separate Morita equivalences with endopermutation source from $p$-permutation equivalences and splendid Rickard equivalences, and also separate almost global isotypies from global isotypies.

papers.title: Sum-of-Squares Certificates for Copositive Matrices via Recursive Identities: The de Klerk-Pasechnik Conjecture and Hoffman-Pereira Matrices
papers.abstract: We establish the conjecture by de Klerk and Pasechnik (2002), claiming that the semidefinite bounds $\vartheta^{(r)}(G)(r\geq 0)$ for the stability number $\alpha(G)$ are exact at $r=\alpha(G)-1$, by exhibiting an explicit sum-of-squares certificate. This certificate allows us to recover a known characterization of the minimizers of the Motzkin-Straus formulation for $1/\alpha(G)$. Additionally, we give sum-of-squares copositivity certificates for the matrices satisfying the Hoffman-Pereira sign condition, a crucial condition for characterizing copositive matrices with $\{-1,0,1\}$ entries.

papers.title: Singular equivalences of $n$-adjoint type and standard eventually homological isomorphisms
papers.authors: Yang Han, Yongyun Qin, Xianqing Wang
papers.abstract: We refine the definition of eventually homological isomorphisms so that it becomes more natural and fruitful. We introduce singular equivalences of $n$-adjoint type which can be viewed as standard singular equivalences of different levels and are more convenient for reducing various homological conjectures and transferring homological properties. We develop the theories of singular equivalences of $n$-adjoint type for $n\ge 2$ and standard eventually homological isomorphisms between derived categories by giving their characterizations in terms of $\otimes$-(co)perfect complexes of bimodules, two constructions via opposite algebras and tensor product algebras, examples induced by homomorphisms of algebras and idempotents, and applications to the reduction of homological conjectures such as the finitistic dimension conjecture, Gorenstein symmetry conjecture and Auslander-Reiten conjecture, as well as to the preservation of homological properties such as Gorensteinness, the Fg condition, Happel's property and Han's property. Moreover, we show that essentially surjective standard eventually homological isomorphisms between derived categories correspond to standard singular equivalences with canonical left adjoint.

papers.title: Iterative construction of the R-matrices in arbitrary dimensions
papers.abstract:
We investigate a special ansats that allows for an iterative solution of the constant Yang-Baxter equation. Testing this ansatz, we construct four sequences of the constant R-matrices. In each sequence the R-matrices act on the tensor squares of vector spaces of linearly growing dimensions. Each R-matrix also depends on a single complex parameter.
  By analyzing the spectra of the R-matrices, we conclude that the first and the third series are associated with the symmetric tensor representations of the quantum groups U_q(sl(2)) and U_q(sl(2|1)), respectively. The other two series appear to be related to representations of quantum groups in the case where q is a root of unity. The elements of the second series are associated with nilpotent representations of U_q(sl(2)).
  We also check the correspondence between these R-matrices and link invariants. Applying the Reshetikhin-Turaev procedure to the first, second, and fourth sequences yields, respectively, colored Jones polynomials, ADO invariants, and Alexander polynomials. To our surprise, a similar calculation for the third series yields a trivial result, identically equal to 1.

papers.title: Yau's conjecture for the stacked Clifford tori of Wiygul
papers.abstract: We prove Yau's conjecture $\lambda_{1}=2$ for the stacked Clifford tori of Wiygul: for all integers $N\ge2$, $k,\ell\ge1$ and every sufficiently large $m$, every closed embedded minimal surface arising from Wiygul's construction, of genus $k\ell m^{2}(N-1)+1$ in the round three-sphere and resembling $N$ parallel copies of the Clifford torus joined by small catenoidal tunnels, has first Laplace eigenvalue $2$. For $N\ge3$ these surfaces are chains rather than doublings, and the even--odd decomposition on which all previous verifications for gluing constructions rest is not available. The reflection lemma of Choe and Soret reduces the problem to the sector of functions invariant under the symmetry group of the construction, and we show that the lowest nonzero eigenvalue of that sector equals $4+O(m^{-1})$. The value $4$ is the outcome of an exact identity in the limiting weighted graph model: the limiting waist ratios of the construction form the Perron vector of the adjacency operator of the line graph of a path, so that the spectral gap of the path cancels against the total conductance of the tunnels prescribed by the balancing conditions, and what survives is the coefficient of the Jacobi operator of the Clifford torus. The analytic input consists of a conformally invariant channel inequality on a cylinder and of a Poincar\'e inequality on a periodically perforated torus. The properties of the construction on which the argument rests are isolated in a reduction theorem for closed surfaces decomposed into blocks joined by families of thin channels along the edges of a finite graph, subject to a symmetry assumption and to Poincar\'e and trace inequalities on the blocks.

papers.title: Unique ergodicity, and not, for primitive substitutions on compact alphabets containing isolated points
papers.abstract: We consider generalised subshifts generated by continuous substitution on compact Hausdorff alphabets. Although primitivity still implies minimality of the subshift generated by the substitution, Durand, Ormes and Petite showed, in contrast to the finite case, that primitivity no longer implies unique ergodicity, by constructing counterexamples with Cantor alphabet. Here we show that, even for the arguably simplest case of the one-point compactification of the natural numbers, primitivity is still insufficient for unique ergodicity, or even the existence of a natural length function (NLF). In previous work with Ma\~{n}ibo and Rust we showed that, for irreducible substitutions, unique ergodicity and existence of a NLF follow from strong power convergence of the renormalised substitution operator \(T\); criteria were also developed that can sometimes confirm strong power convergence. Here we show the converse, so that strong power convergence of \(T\) is equivalent to having both unique ergodicity and a NLF. We then consider the case of alphabets with only finitely many accumulation points, showing how upper bounds (and usually an exact formula) for the essential spectral radius of \(T\) can be derived from associated finite substitutions, determined by the behaviour of substitution of the accumulation points. For many primitive substitutions this can be used to prove quasi-compactness of \(T\), and thus unique ergodicity. For primitive substitutions on alphabets with at least one isolated point, we show that strong power convergence and quasi-compactness of \(T\) are equivalent and, in fact, that these properties are equivalent to iteration of substitution growing words in length uniformly across all seeds in the alphabet.

papers.title: The Loopy Polynomial: from Tutte's Universal $V$-Function to Bizonotopal Geometry
papers.authors: Anatol Kirillov, Gleb Nenashev, Boris Shapiro, Arkady Vaintrob
papers.abstract:
We study the loopy polynomial L_G, a multivariate graph invariant arising from bizonotopal graphical algebras and defined by deletion and loopy contraction, in which the contracted edge is retained as a loop. It determines the Tutte polynomial and admits a spanning-forest expansion recording external activity componentwise. It also determines Stanley's chromatic symmetric function for every graph; the degree sequence, induced edge count profile, and independence polynomial for loopless graphs; and the clique and matching polynomials for simple graphs. Separating component size from external activity gives a refinement that is equivalent to the extended U-polynomial and the extended polychromate. The ordinary U-polynomial, Tutte's universal $V$-function, and Stanley's Tutte symmetric function are specializations of this refinement.
  We conjecture that L_G and U_G have the same distinguishing power on simple graphs, and verify this through eleven vertices. We exhibit five-vertex loopless multigraphs with equal U-polynomials but distinct loopy and extended U-polynomials, solving a problem of Merino and Noble. We also disprove Loebl's conjecture for chordal graphs and its restriction to split graphs, with counterexamples on eleven and fourteen vertices, respectively.
  For the score polytope P_G of the external bizonotopal algebra, we give a geometric realization of loopy deletion-contraction. The resulting forest-indexed geometric parking complexes partition the lattice points of P_G and are piecewise integral-affinely parametrized by boxes whose interval lengths are the component indices in the forest expansion.

papers.title: Gromov-Hausdorff Distances Between Spheres: Asymptotics and Vietoris-Rips Coindex Bounds
papers.authors: Sunhyuk Lim, Facundo M\'emoli, Qingsong Wang
papers.abstract: For $1\le m<n$, let $c_{m,n}$ be the infimum of the scales $r$ at which the Vietoris-Rips simplicial complex of the unit round sphere $\mathbb{S}^m$, equipped with its geodesic metric, admits a continuous odd map from $\mathbb{S}^n$. Previous work established the lower bound $\frac{1}{2}c_{m,n}\le d_{\mathrm{GH}}(\mathbb{S}^m,\mathbb{S}^n)$ through a quantitative Borsuk-Ulam theorem and raised the question of whether it is always sharp. We show that this bound can underestimate the distance by a factor arbitrarily close to two, the largest possible factor. Combining projective-code upper bounds for $c_{m,n}$ with lower bounds for $d_{\mathrm{GH}}$ obtained from obstructions to homomorphisms between Borsuk graphs, we obtain explicit finite-dimensional bounds. Along sequences of pairs $1\le m<n$, we have $c_{m,n}\to\frac{\pi}{2}$ whenever $\log n/m\to0$, while $d_{\mathrm{GH}}(\mathbb{S}^m,\mathbb{S}^n)\to\frac{\pi}{2}$ whenever $m/n\to0$. When both conditions hold (for example when $n=m^2$) the ratio of the distance to $\frac{1}{2}c_{m,n}$ tends to two. For each fixed $m\ge3$, the inequality is strict for all sufficiently large $n$.

papers.title: A counterexample to Kenig's conjecture for the Laplace double-layer operator
papers.abstract: We disprove Kenig's 1994 spectral-radius conjecture for the double-layer operator in every dimension $d\ge2$. For every $t>1/2$ sufficiently close to $1/2$, we construct a bounded simply connected Lipschitz domain with connected boundary such that the double-layer operator on $L^2$ with respect to the surface measure has $\pm \mathrm{i} t$ in its Fredholm essential spectrum. In particular, the essential spectral radius is greater than $1/2$. In the plane, the boundary may be chosen differentiable everywhere and smooth away from a single point. Our planar construction develops a refinement mechanism that produces unbounded growth of adjoint resolvent solutions with fixed forcing while keeping the graph slopes uniformly bounded. A closed recursion for the density and its image under an auxiliary singular integral reduces the growth estimate to a certified inequality for Hermitian $2\times2$ matrices. The certificate uses continuous estimates, exact rational arithmetic and rigorous interval enclosures. Localisation and rescaled graph insertions then produce a weakly null sequence of normalised approximate eigenvectors for the adjoint double-layer operator on one bounded boundary. A compact intertwining relation on Cartesian products of the planar domain with cubes gives the higher-dimensional examples without changing the spectral parameter.

papers.title: Regular Arithmetic Functions, Volume I. Theory, Applications, Examples
papers.abstract:
This is the first of two volumes on regular arithmetic functions, and an introduction to their theory.
  A regular arithmetic function (RAF) is a kernel whose properties come from a single defining equation. Let $G(n,k)$ be a function of two integer variables with $G(n,n)\neq 0$, and for each $\beta$ define a sequence $(a_k)$ by $\sum_{k\le n} a_k G(n,k)=n^{-\beta}$, solved rank by rank with nothing to assume and no convergence to establish. Then $G$ is regular when the partial sums $\sum_{k\le n} a_k$ change behaviour at one exponent. Below it they reproduce the forced rate, above it they absorb it. That tipping point is the regularity index $\alpha(G)$, a quantity belonging to the kernel itself.
  The index came out of analogies, experiment and observation, and it is arithmetic by nature. Its most visible application is the Riemann hypothesis, which holds if and only if Ingham's kernel $G(n,k)=(k/n)\lfloor n/k\rfloor$ is a RAF of index $1/2$. It is not the only one. On a problem of a quite different kind the same theory improves the known decay bound for the orthorecursive expansion of unity. Seventeen kernels are worked out in a gallery, so that the notion can be handled by the reader. What is conjectural, conditional or open is marked as such and collected in a register. Volume II is given over to that kernel alone, with its connection to the world of Hasse-Weil zeta functions through a gauged system.

papers.title: Regularity for Subfactors
papers.abstract: We study three naturally associated notions of regularity for a unital inclusion of von Neumann algebras $\mathcal{B} \subseteq \mathcal{M}$: regularity, groupoid regularity, and unitary regularity. We first observe that regularity and groupoid regularity are unconditionally equivalent by showing that the standard normaliser and the groupoid normaliser of $\mathcal{B}$ in $\mathcal M$ generate the same linear span. The central question addressed in this work is whether regularity implies unitary regularity. For arbitrary von Neumann subalgebras, we demonstrate that this implication fails dramatically; we construct explicit examples to show that every factor (of type $\mathrm{I}_\infty$, $\mathrm{II}_1$, $\mathrm{II}_\infty$, and $\mathrm{III}$) contains a regular von Neumann subalgebra that is not unitarily regular. In stark contrast, we prove that the behaviour changes completely in the setting of subfactors. For subfactor inclusions across all these types, regularity always implies unitary regularity, and thus all three notions of regularity coincide.

papers.title: Birational cubic fourfolds via an Enriques Cremona transformation
papers.abstract: We describe a Cremona transformation on $\mathbb{P}^5$ given by the linear system of quintics that are double along the Fano model of an Enriques surface $S$. Using this Cremona transform, we construct a birational equivalence between the very general cubic fourfold $X$ of discriminant 44 and its unique Fourier--Mukai partner. We also classify birational maps between smooth, non-isomorphic cubic fourfolds resolved by blowing up a smooth surface on each side: the centres must be either Fano models of Enriques surfaces, as in our construction, or Veronese surfaces, as studied by Fan--Lai.

papers.title: Lateral Weak Stieltjes Derivatives: A Global Characterization of Stieltjes--Sobolev Spaces
papers.abstract: Weak formulations for Stieltjes differential equations must retain the directional information carried by atoms of the driving measure. We derive a lateral integration-by-parts identity in which the posterior trace of the test function is forced by the atomic product rule. The resulting dual formulation gives an exact global characterization of integral Stieltjes--Sobolev spaces for the full exponent range from one to infinity and reconstructs the unique strong representative from its traced weak state. We prove that the associated traced weak operator is closed, establish Poincar\'e--Stieltjes estimates, and \rev{characterize Stieltjes absolute continuity inside bounded variation through a canonical derivative measure whose restriction to the open interval is the classical distributional derivative}. The framework is then applied to finite-dimensional nonlinear measure-driven systems, yielding equivalence of weak, integral, and measure formulations, existence and uniqueness under integrable Lipschitz assumptions, compactness-based existence, and intrinsic reset laws. Cubic and logistic models illustrate the simultaneous encoding of continuous evolution and instantaneous interventions.

papers.title: Well-Defined but Not Predetermined Persistent Mathematical Objects, Embedded Observers, and the Provability of P = N P
papers.abstract:
We develop a foundational distinction between \emph{well-definedness} and \emph{predetermination}. A persistent mathematical or computational object may return a unique answer whenever a query is made and preserve every previously returned answer, while its answers to as-yet unqueried inputs are not represented by one completed, history-independent extension. We call such an object \emph{well-defined but non-predetermined}.
  We next formulate an observer-based semantics. All observers inhabit one shared computational world, their interactions modify one common global state, and they have access to one realized history. Under axioms of shared history, historical irreversibility, persistence, and historical indistinguishability, embedded observers cannot establish from the realized history alone whether its compatible extension was predetermined or progressively formed. A persistently evolutionary polynomial time computable oracle supplies a concrete example and yields a deterministic--nondeterministic separation under an explicitly history-sensitive semantics. We then derive a conditional result concerning the provability of \(P=NP\). The conclusion is an observer-relative unprovability theorem, not an unconditional proof of classical \(P\neq NP\).

papers.title: Elementary modal logics and circuit complexity
papers.abstract: A modal logic is elementary if it is sound and complete with respect to an elementary class of Kripke frames. We prove that if a finitely axiomatizable modal logic $L$ is elementary, then the validity problem for $L$, which asks whether a given finite Kripke frame validates $L$, is in the circuit complexity class uniform $\mathsf{AC}^0$. As an application, we construct infinitely many finitely axiomatizable $\mathsf{K4}$-stable logics that are not elementary. This result provides a negative answer to Problem 6.4 in [Bezhanishvili et al., 2018] for $\mathsf{K4}$-stable logics.

papers.title: Strong Consistency, Optimal Tracking and Sharp Rates for the {\AA}str\"om-Wittenmark Self-Tuning Regulator with Unknown Input Gain
papers.abstract: We study strong consistency and optimal tracking of the Astrom-Wittenmark self-tuning regulator with unknown input gain. Existing results establish consistency of all parameter estimates for the unmodified recursion under additional growth conditions on reference information. Other approaches obtain stability and optimal tracking by adjusting the estimates used in feedback or adding decaying probing signals. For a class of minimum-phase linear systems with martingale difference noise, ordinary least squares (LS) with certainty-equivalent control achieves stability and optimal tracking almost surely for each bounded reference, provided the recursion is well defined. No reference excitation, adjustment of feedback estimates or added probing is required. When at least two parameters are estimated, all parameter estimates are strongly consistent, with squared norm of the estimation error $O(\log\log\log n/\log n)$ almost surely. A law of the iterated logarithm under zero reference shows that this rate cannot in general be improved. We also derive a logarithm law for cumulative squared tracking residuals, with an explicit dependence of the leading term on reference energy. A chi-square limit yields asymptotically exact parameter confidence ellipsoids for each bounded reference. The proof combines a logarithmic lower bound on the cumulative squared difference between an auxiliary LS prediction of the noise and the reference with estimates from the LS recursion. If the gain estimate were inconsistent, these bounds would yield incompatible estimates for the same weighted sum of squares, establishing gain consistency without assuming stability.

papers.title: The Chern character of a coherent sheaf on a smooth projective hypersurface
papers.abstract: Given a coherent sheaf on a smooth projective hypersurface X, we prove an explicit formula for its Chern character as a Cech cocycle in terms of the free resolution of the associated module and calculate its image in the Jacobian ring under the Griffiths residue map. The formula is a geometric analogue of the Kapustin-Li formula for Landau-Ginzburg models, but proven directly using Hodge-theoretic techniques. This yields an effective method to compute the primitive part of the Chern character of any coherent sheaf using commutative algebra. We finish by proving the Hodge conjecture for the degree 33 Fermat fourfold.

papers.title: Sharp Linear Bounds and Exponential Separation for Single-Flip Methods in Absolute Value Equations
papers.abstract: Rohn's sign-accord algorithm is a classical single-coordinate sign-flip method for $Ax-|x|=b$, selecting the least-index mismatched coordinate at each step. We construct rational instances on which this rule requires exactly $2^{n-1}-1$ flips from natural initialization, even when both $\|A^{-1}\|_1$ and $\|A^{-1}\|_\infty$ are arbitrarily small. We propose two alternative selection rules, Gauss--Southwell and steepest single flipping, which require only one flip on the same instances. A discrete potential framework with positive polarity factors identifies solutions with global maximizers. Under positive polarity with ratio $\kappa$ and $r=\|A^{-1}\|_\infty<1$, both rules terminate from any initial signature after at most $\lfloor s\kappa(1+r)/(1-r)\rfloor$ flips, where $s$ is the number of nonzero solution coordinates. For fixed $\eta_1<1/2$ and $\eta_2<1$, both rules have worst-case flip complexity $O(n)$ on the class $\|A^{-1}\|_1\le\eta_1$ and $\|A^{-1}\|_\infty\le\eta_2$. An $n-1$ lower bound from natural initialization shows that this linear order is sharp. Under stronger, explicit sign-correction conditions, each rule makes exactly as many flips as there are initially incorrect signs among the nonzero solution components. Thus, each rule makes at most \(n\) flips, and this bound is optimal. A five-dimensional example requiring six greedy flips shows that the bound of $n$ does not extend to the entire common small-norm class. Building on Radons--Rump sign certificates, we further develop three classes of sign-flip algorithms using elimination guidance, cyclic scanning, and randomized $m$-flipping. Under $\rho(|A^{-1}|)<1/2$, we prove at most $n$ flips for elimination guidance, $n^2$ inspections for cyclic scanning, and $O(n^2/m)$ expected batch updates for randomized $m$-flipping. Exact computations and retained paired experiments distinguish flip counts from computational cost.

papers.title: Matching Higher-Order Oracle Complexity for Smooth Monotone Variational Inequalities
papers.authors: Haihan Zhang, Wendao Wu, Chenheng Zhang, Cong Fang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin
papers.abstract: We establish near-optimal higher-order oracle bounds for smooth monotone variational inequalities. For fixed $p\ge2$, let $F$ be monotone on a known compact convex set $X$ of diameter at most $D$, with $\operatorname{Lip}(D^{p-1}F)\le L_p$. Each feasible query returns the complete jet $(F,DF,\ldots,D^{p-1}F)$, and the goal is to find $x$ with tangent residual $\operatorname{dist}(0,F(x)+N_X(x))\le\varepsilon$. Writing $Q=L_pD^p/\varepsilon$, we improve the $\widetilde O_p(Q^{1/p})$ upper bound of Chen et al. to $\widetilde O_p(Q^{2/(3p-1)})$ via a dimension-independent deterministic algorithm that returns an explicit tangent-residual certificate. We prove a matching $\Omega_p(Q^{2/(3p-1)})$ lower bound for arbitrary adaptive deterministic algorithms and randomized algorithms with per-instance success probability at least $2/3$, without span or tensor-update restrictions. Hence the high-dimensional worst-case oracle complexity is $\widetilde\Theta_p((L_pD^p/\varepsilon)^{2/(3p-1)})$. The same method applies to smooth convex--concave minimax problems, improving the fixed-geometry accuracy exponent from $4/(3p+1)$ to $2/(3p-1)$ and matching the known lower-bound exponent.

papers.title: Single commutators in $C^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal A$ be a simple unital $C^*$-algebra with real rank zero, nonempty tracial state space $\mathcal T(\mathcal A)$, and strict comparison of projections. We prove that every element $T$ in $\mathcal A$ with $\tau(T)=0$ for all $\tau\in\mathcal T(\mathcal A)$ is a single commutator if one of the following conditions holds: $(1)$ $\mathcal A$ has unique trace; $(2)$ $\mathcal A$ has stable rank one. We also prove that every nonscalar element in a simple unital purely infinite $C^*$-algebra is a single commutator. Applications include UHF algebras, irrational rotation algebras, and Cuntz algebras.

papers.title: Invasion dynamics with vanishing fitness for a quasi-critical birth-death process
papers.authors: Vincent Bansaye, Nadia Belmabrouk, Xavier Erny, Simon Girel
papers.abstract: We study the invasion dynamics of populations exhibiting positive density-dependent effects. We start with a single individual and consider a single-type birth and death process. The initial individual growth rate vanishes but it increases with the population density, proportionally to the number of individuals divided by a scaling parameter $K$. Before reaching the macroscopic scale~$K$, the population process is almost critical. We prove that the probability for the population to reach the macroscopic level $K$ decreases as $1/\sqrt{K}$ as $K$ goes to infinity. We also describe the associated trajectories and show that invasion can be split into three time periods. First, the process needs to escape from zero, and conditioning on survival, it grows linearly until the order $\sqrt{K}$. The scaled process is approximated by a diffusion, as for critical branching process, with an additional drift term coming from cooperation, which breaks the branching property. Second, in intermediate scale $\sqrt{K}$, we observe another diffusion, surviving with positive probability, without conditioning. Finally, beyond $\sqrt{K}$ scale, the process can be approximated by a classical macroscopic ODE limit. The proof of the first phase involves change of probability and characterization of uniform integrability of martingales, while the two other phases rely on uniform approximations on polynomial time scales.

papers.title: Integral cohomology of classical Artin groups: spherical types $A,C,D$ and affine types $\widetilde B,\widetilde C,\widetilde D$
papers.abstract: We determine the additive structure of the integral cohomology groups with trivial coefficients of the Artin groups in the spherical families $A_n,C_n,D_n$ and the affine families $\widetilde B_n,\widetilde C_n,\widetilde D_n$. We first compute the integral cohomology of braid groups by algebraic methods and then use the Salvetti complexes to express the cohomology of the remaining families in terms of these computations. The resulting descriptions apply in every admissible rank. For each family, we establish cohomological stabilization and show that the integral cohomology groups contain no elements of order $p^2$ for any prime $p$. We also give uniform generating series formulas describing the stable integral cohomology in terms of that of the braid groups.

papers.title: Dimension-dependent symmetry breaking in a diffusive nonlocal interaction model
papers.authors: Dohyun Kim, Hansol Park, Woojoo Shim
papers.abstract: We study the equilibrium structure and long-time behavior of a nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation with diffusion and nonlocal interactions generated by squared simplex volumes. For $1\leq n<d$, the stationary states are isotropic Gaussian measures, and every solution converges to the equilibrium determined by its conserved mean. At $n=d$, the free energy fixes only the covariance determinant, allowing a continuum of anisotropic Gaussian equilibria when $d\geq2$. We establish global well-posedness for arbitrary initial probability measures with finite second moment, identify stationary states with the global minimizers of the free energy, and prove convergence in quadratic Wasserstein distance with explicit exponential rates.

papers.title: Representations of solutions to Stein equations and their derivatives
papers.abstract: We propose pointwise representations of the Stein solution to a weighted first-order Stein equation associated with a univariate absolutely continuous distribution. The representation extends to all the derivatives of the solution and with respect to any derivative of the test function. The mechanism behind these representations is an array of kernels that satisfy two key identities, yielding a specific calculus for the Stein framework considered here. The representations record every correction term appearing by differentiation, explaining how choosing the Stein kernel as weight has a special role in Taylor and pairing arguments. The calculus of the kernel extends these representations to any order and exhibits natural and explicit conditions to obtain a one term representation of the $n$-th derivative of the solution with respect to exactly one of the three neighbouring test-function orders of derivatives, \(n-1,n,n+1\). These conditions are simple to ensure by choosing the weight accordingly. The representations yield pointwise envelopes, uniform and weighted Stein factors, and ensure sharpness of the constants. We recover the known sharp results for the Gaussian and the Gamma distribution, improve known factors for the rest of the integrated Pearson family, which is the family under which every correction term cancels. We also study the Subbotin and symmetrized Maxwell families, for which the formulas retain additional pointwise terms. Applications sharpen constants in known distributional approximations and use the higher-order calculus to obtain Edgeworth corrections for the Beta approximation of the P\'olya--Eggenberger urn and the quartic Subbotin approximation in the critical Curie--Weiss model.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Deterministic Exact-Value Complexity for Smooth Convex Optimization
papers.authors: Wendao Wu, Haihan Zhang, Chenheng Zhang, Yanyi Li, Chunyuan Zheng, Cong Fang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin
papers.abstract: We study the deterministic oracle complexity of smooth convex optimization when the algorithm receives only exact function values. The objective is a globally $\beta$-smooth convex function, all queries and the final output are restricted to the Euclidean ball of radius $R$, and the unique minimizer lies in the ball of radius $R/2$. We establish an upper bound of $O(d\sqrt{\beta R^2/\epsilon})$ using coordinate finite differences together with an error-robust accelerated projected method. Our main contribution is a matching lower bound, up to the high-accuracy saturation of the construction: any deterministic adaptive value-oracle algorithm requires $\Omega\!\left(d\min\{\sqrt{\beta R^2/\epsilon},(d/\log(ed))^{1/3}\}\right)$ queries. Consequently, the minimax oracle complexity is $\Theta(d\sqrt{\beta R^2/\epsilon})$ throughout the moderate-accuracy regime $\beta R^2(\log(ed)/d)^{2/3}\leq\epsilon\leq c\beta R^2$ for a universal constant $c>0$. The lower bound must account for the fact that a single exact real value can encode arbitrarily much information. To overcome this difficulty, we construct a single fixed smooth convex hard instance using a Moreau-smoothed biased max chain, an exact prefix-shielding mechanism, and batched delayed rotations. These techniques preserve consistency with the full adaptive transcript and establish the optimality of the square-root complexity branch for deterministic bounded-query algorithms.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Exact-Value Zeroth-Order Complexity for Smooth Strongly Convex Optimization
papers.authors: Wendao Wu, Haihan Zhang, Chenheng Zhang, Yanyi Li, Chunyuan Zheng, Cong Fang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin
papers.abstract: We study deterministic adaptive optimization of globally $\beta$-smooth, $\mu$-strongly convex functions using exact scalar function values. Queries and outputs lie in $B_2^d(R)$, and the minimizer lies in $B_2^d(R/2)$. Set $\kappa=\beta/\mu$, $Q=\beta R^2/\epsilon$, and $D_d=(d/\log(ed))^{1/3}$. For sufficiently large $d$ and $0<\epsilon\le c_\epsilon\beta R^2$, the minimax value complexity $N_\epsilon$ satisfies \[ \begin{aligned} N_\epsilon &\ge c d\min\{\sqrt Q,\sqrt\kappa,D_d\},\\ N_\epsilon &\le C d\min\left\{ \sqrt Q,\sqrt\kappa[1+\log_+(Q/\kappa)] \right\}, \end{aligned} \] where $c,C,c_\epsilon>0$ are universal constants and $\log_+(t)=\max\{0,\log t\}$. The lower bound uses an exactly shielded smooth chain and batched delayed rotations; the upper bound combines finite differences, acceleration, and restart. When $\min\{Q,\kappa\}\le D_d^2$, these bounds match up to constants in the accuracy-dominated regime $Q\le\kappa$ and at constant relative accuracy $\epsilon=\Theta(\mu R^2)$. For arbitrarily higher accuracy in the range $\kappa\le D_d^2$, the bounds differ by at most $1+\log(\mu R^2/\epsilon)$; the optimal accuracy dependence remains unresolved in general.

papers.title: Polynomial rigidity of strong-field magnetic billiards
papers.abstract:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded domain whose boundary $\gamma$ is a smooth simple closed curve, and let $r=|B|^{-1}$ be the Larmor radius of a constant magnetic field. Assume $$ 0<r<\frac{r_0(\gamma)}2, $$ where $r_0(\gamma)$ is the maximal embedded tubular radius of $\gamma$. We prove that if the corresponding magnetic billiard admits a nonconstant first integral polynomial in the velocity, then $\gamma$ is a circle and $\Omega$ is a disk. No convexity assumption is imposed.
  This eliminates the finite set of possible exceptional strong-field values left by the earlier polynomial nonintegrability theory. The proof uses the two highest reflection modes of the polynomial induced on the space of Larmor centers. A boundary index identity shows that the highest coefficient has degree equal to the true Fourier degree and that all of its roots lie inside the table. After complexification and passage to the normalization of the boundary curve, comparison of the two leading modes at infinity excludes simultaneous poles of the coordinate functions and forces all of these roots to coincide. The reflection identity then implies that the boundary has constant distance from their common root and hence is circular.

papers.title: Separable quotients of pointwise function spaces and relative consistency
papers.abstract: Assuming Jensen's diamond principle, we construct a separable crowded compact zero-dimensional space $K$ of weight $\aleph_1$ and cardinality $2^{\aleph_1}$ such that $C_p(K)$ has no infinite-dimensional Hausdorff separable linear quotient. In particular, $K$ is an Efimov space: it contains neither a nontrivial convergent sequence nor a copy of $\beta\mathbb N$. We also prove in ZFC that the existence of a separable quotient of this kind is equivalent to the existence of a metrisable one. On the positive side, established finite-support random-sign methods give a split quotient of $C_p(K)$ onto $(c_0)_p$ whenever $K$ is infinite compact and $w(K)<\operatorname{cov}\mathcal N$, with explicit norm-one operators. Consequently, the universal quotient assertion for compacta of weight $\aleph_1$ is independent relative to the consistency of ZFC alone. A real-valued measurable continuum gives the positive result below the continuum and reduces the remaining problem to separable compacta of weight exactly the continuum. The counterexample uses direct diamond prediction, a simultaneous successor lemma, and a compactness argument converting localised measure limits into differences of point masses.

papers.title: Polynomially larger deletion codes by linear hashing of substring counts
papers.abstract: We reduce the leading redundancy coefficient for binary codes correcting any fixed number $t\ge2$ of deletions from $2t$ to $2t-1$. This is the first improvement to that coefficient since Levenshtein's 1965 bound. More generally, over every fixed alphabet of size $q\ge2$, codes of length $n$ correcting any combination of at most $t$ insertions, deletions and substitutions exist with redundancy $(2t-1)\log_q n+O_t(\log_q\log_q n)$. For two deletions, the upper-bound coefficient drops from $4$ to $3$, halving the gap to the lower-bound coefficient $2$. The leading coefficient $2t-1$ also holds for $t$ bounded substring edits, where both the removed and inserted strings have bounded length. The proof combines random binary linear hashing of substring counts with a two-colouring argument. A linear dependence among differences of substring-count vectors forces their local changes to overlap, and this overlap lowers the redundancy coefficient from $2t$ to $2t-1$. The result provides an edit-distance analogue of Varshamov's 1957 bound in the Hamming metric, both in the leading redundancy coefficient and in the role of linear independence in the proof.

papers.title: Chow Vanishing and Motives of Cluster Varieties
papers.abstract: We prove that the integral Chow groups $CH_i$ and mixed Hodge degree $H^{2i, (i, i)}$ cohomology groups of a really full rank (RFR) sink-recurrent cluster variety vanish for $i > 0$. In particular this applies to braid varieties and open projected Richardson varieties in any Lie type. Our main technical tool is the construction of a stratification of any RFR sink-recurrent cluster variety $\mathcal{A}(\Sigma)$ over any field $k$ into (affine space times) RFR sink-recurrent cluster varieties of seeds with fewer mutable vertices than $\Sigma$, with which we show that RFR sink-recurrent cluster varieties are linear in the sense of Totaro. We also show that cycle class maps are isomorphisms onto the lowest-weight part of rational Borel-Moore homology for any mixed Tate variety over a number field. Finally, we use our results to deduce vanishing theorems for the Khovanov-Rozansky homology groups of closures of positive braids and generation properties for the Chow groups of flag Richardson, projected Richardson, and brick varieties: namely, that these groups are generated integrally by the fundamental classes of their closed Richardson, positroid, and braid strata, respectively.

papers.title: Bounds for Codimension-One Components of Zero Loci of Bernstein-Sato Ideals
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth complex affine variety of dimension $n$, and let $F=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ be a tuple of nonzero regular functions on $X$ such that $f:=\prod_{i=1}^r f_i$ is not invertible. We study the zero loci of the Bernstein-Sato ideals $B_F^{\mathbf a}$ for nonnegative integral shifts $\mathbf a$. For a fixed log resolution, every codimension-one irreducible component of $Z(B_F^{\mathbf a})$ is a hyperplane of the form $L_E(\mathbf s)+k_E+c=0$ with $c$ a positive integer. We give a new proof of this result using localized maximal and minimal extensions of relative D-modules. We also prove that $c\leq L_E(\mathbf a)+(n-1-\delta_f)L_E(\mathbf 1)-k_E$, where $\delta_f=\min\{n-1,\alpha_f\}$ and $\alpha_f$ is the minimal exponent of $f$. The problem of obtaining such an upper bound for arbitrary tuples (in particular, for $r>1$) was raised by Budur, van der Veer, and Van Werde, and the above inequality resolves it. To obtain the upper bound, we compare the diagonal slice of $Z(B_F^{\mathbf 1})$ with the root set of $b_f$. A finite covering by translates, combined with diagonal specialization and the log-resolution description, shows that these sets have the same least and greatest points. Saito's root estimate at their common least point then yields the upper bound. We further establish a divisor-valued formulation of the local index comparison, recovering the detection of monodromy support via monodromy zeta functions and the multivariable A'Campo formula.

papers.title: Multidimensional fractional material derivative: measure-valued solutions and probabilistic properties
papers.abstract: We analyze a nonlocal operator in space and time, called the multidimensional fractional material derivative. We derive its pointwise representation, which allows us to study its other properties. We define an inverse operator, called fractional material integral, and derive its pointwise representation. Furthermore, we analyze a class of linear partial differential equations, which corresponds to deterministic descriptions of the scaling limits of multidimensional L\'evy walks, in which transport is driven by a multidimensional fractional material derivative with a speed vector integrated with respect to a suitable probability measure and a distributional source term. Using Fourier-Laplace transform techniques and a direct convolution-kernel construction, we prove the existence and uniqueness of exponentially integrable measure solutions for measure data. Moreover, we identify a necessary and sufficient condition on the source term for conservation of unit mass and provide separate sufficient conditions for non-negativity and weak convergence to $\delta_0$. We also prove weak continuity and self-similarity of the kernel and continuous dependence on the directional distribution.

papers.title: Four Special Directions over Prime Fields: Structure and Complete Classification
papers.abstract: A direction of the affine plane $\mathbb{F}_p^2$ is special for a set if the lines in that direction do not all meet the set in the same number of points. We classify, for every prime $p\ge5$, the subsets of $\mathbb{F}_p^2$ with exactly four special directions. There are $54$ affine-equivalence classes, occurring only for $p=5,7,11,13,17$, and we give explicit representatives. In particular, $17$ is the largest prime admitting such a set, which answers a question of Ghidelli, Kiss and Somlai, and over $\mathbb{F}_{13}$ the minimum size is $65$, attained by exactly two classes. The key structural fact is that the projection polynomials of such a set share a vertex: the set is either centrally symmetric about this point or differs from its reflection by exchanging one full line with one empty line. We also show that, over an odd prime field, a Boolean function on $\mathbb{F}_p^d$ with exactly four active projective Fourier lines is pulled back from a plane, so the classification extends to every dimension. The classification and the exclusion of the primes $19\le p<2048$ are computer-assisted; the structural results and the exclusion of larger primes are proved directly.

papers.title: Wild frieze patterns over the integers
papers.abstract: We study frieze patterns over the integers that are allowed to have wild entries. We introduce the quiddity number as a new invariant. The quiddity number is then used to classify strongly connected components of the directed graph $\Gamma_{2,n}(\mathbb{Z})$. Furthermore, we show that every finite simple directed graph arises as an induced subgraph of a directed graph $\Gamma_{2,n}(\mathbb{Z})$ for $n$ sufficiently large.

papers.title: Gaussian fluctuations for the stochastic wave equation with drift
papers.authors: Raluca M. Balan, William D. Stephenson
papers.abstract: In this article, we study the spatial fluctuations of the solution to the stochastic wave equation with a nonlinear drift and multiplicative Gaussian noise in dimensions one and two. The noise is white in time, and its spatial covariance is either integrable or given by a Riesz kernel; space-time white noise in dimension one is also included. We establish spatial ergodicity, convergence of the rescaled covariance, and prove a quantitative central limit theorem for the spatial fluctuations. We also obtain the corresponding functional central limit theorem. Our approach exploits the compact support of the wave kernel to obtain an estimate for the spatially integrated second Malliavin derivative which is compatible with a bound for the total variation. Further arguments based on the Clark-Ocone formula are used to control the drift contributions.

papers.title: Macdonald principal specialization ratios and their generating polynomials
papers.abstract: We establish independence of $q$ as a necessary condition for coefficientwise nonnegativity of normalized principal specialization ratios of monic Macdonald polynomials. For arbitrary pairs of partitions, we characterize independence of $q$. For denominator partitions with largest and smallest parts differing by at least two, every ratio independent of $q$ is a power of $t$. We classify the nonnegative ratios under addition of maximal rows and columns of fixed height. For rows of length at least two, the classification is equivalent to rectangular complementation. For arbitrary initial partitions, the generating polynomials of successive row ratios at the smallest number of variables admissible for all stages have simple negative real zeros with lower bounds for the ratios of consecutive absolute zeros. We derive a reciprocity criterion, bounds for gamma coefficients, and the corresponding Jack limit. For generalized staircases, we determine shortest horizontal and conjugate vertical strip sequences and obtain terminating basic hypergeometric representations.

papers.title: Admissible $qx+1$ Sequences, Semiconvergents, and Rational Catalan Numbers
papers.abstract: Let $q\geq3$ be odd and put $m_r=\lfloor r\log_2q\rfloor$. We count parity sequences with exactly $r$ odd entries for which the coefficient in the $qx+1$ iteration first drops below $1$ at step $m_r+1$. Their number $a_q(r)$ also counts the corresponding residue classes modulo $2^{m_r+1}$. We derive a first-violation recurrence which, for $q=3$, proves a recurrence conjectured in 2015. We establish the sharp inequalities \[ \frac1r\binom{m_r-1}{r-1}\leq a_q(r)\leq\frac1r\binom{m_r}{r-1}. \] Equality is characterized by the lower and upper record indices of $\{r\log_2q\}$, equivalently by denominators of convergents and semiconvergents from below and above. At these indices $r\geq2$, the values $a_q(r)$ are rational Catalan numbers. We also characterize the dependence on $q$ and prove, for each fixed odd $q\geq3$, that $a_q(r)=\Theta_q(r^{-3/2}B_q^r)$, where $B_q=(\log_2q)^{\log_2q}/(\log_2q-1)^{\log_2q-1}$. For $q=3$, this settles Hikawa's conjecture concerning the polynomial factor in a related counting function.

papers.title: Existence and non-existence of extremal functions for inequalities of Bliss-Moser type
papers.authors: Yanyan Guo, Huxiao Luo, Bernhard Ruf
papers.abstract: We establish a concentration--compactness theory for a one-dimensional singular Moser-type functional with logarithmic weight function $$\sup\limits_{v\in E }\int_0^1 e^{\left(\log\frac{e}{s}+\gamma\log\log\frac{e}{s}\right)\frac{v^2(s)}{s}}ds<\infty,~\gamma\in[0,1],$$ where $$E:= \left\{u \in H^{1}(0, 1): u(0) = 0, \int_0^1 |u'|^2dx=1\right\}.$$ In particular, we prove compactness for all normalized sequences in the subcritical range $\gamma<1$, thereby resolving an open problem proposed in [J. M. do \'{O}, B. Ruf and P. Ubilla, CVPDE 2023]. We also study the critical Bliss-Moser inequality: \begin{equation}\nonumber \sup\limits_{v\in E }I^c(v)< +\infty,\quad I^c(v)=\int_0^1 e^{\left(\log\frac{e}{s}+\log\log\frac{e}{s}+cs\right)\frac{v^2(s)}{s}}ds. \end{equation} For any $c\in(-\infty,+\infty)$, we determine the sharp concentration level $$\sup_{v_j\in E,v_j~\text{is~NCS}}\limsup\limits_{j\to\infty} I^c(v_j)=1+e^2,$$ and obtain explicit sufficient conditions for attainability under $c>c^*$ and non-attainability under $c<-c_*$. This results describe how linear perturbations govern the transition between compactness, concentration, and attainability at the critical level.

papers.title: Localization Lengths for Two-Dimensional Random Band Matrices: Stretched-Exponential Lower Bounds
papers.abstract: We consider $N \times N$ random band matrices $H = (H_{xy})$ with centered complex Gaussian entries, indexed by points $x,y$ on the two-dimensional discrete torus $(\mathbb{Z} / \sqrt{N} \mathbb{Z})^2$. The matrix entries $H_{xy}$ vanish whenever the distance between $x$ and $y$ exceeds a constant multiple of the bandwidth parameter $W$. We prove that, for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$, if $W\geq(\log N)^{2+\varepsilon}$, then all bulk eigenvectors are delocalized with high probability. Equivalently, this yields a lower bound of order $\exp(W^{1/2-\varepsilon})$ on the localization length of two-dimensional random band matrices for arbitrarily small constant $\varepsilon>0$, improving the superpolynomial lower bound $W^C$ for every fixed constant $C>0$ established in arXiv:2503.07606. A key ingredient of our proof is a new strategy that closes the resolvent flow analysis using only loop observables of order at most two, without relying on the higher-order loop hierarchy.

papers.title: Global well-posedness and scattering for the three-dimensional defocusing cubic Schr\"odinger equation in $H^s$, $s>\frac{1}{2}$
papers.abstract: We prove global well-posedness and scattering for the three-dimensional defocusing cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with arbitrary initial data in $H^s(\R^3)$, $s>\frac{1}{2}$, without radial symmetry. The proof combines the $I$-method with long-time $L^2_{t,x}$ bounds for products of frequency-localized components of the nonlinear solution. The key high--low estimate follows from a directional interaction identity pairing high-frequency mass with low-frequency energy, together with an induction on frequency.

papers.title: Exponential improvements in Rado's covering problem
papers.abstract:
Let $B^d$ denote the $d$-dimensional Euclidean ball of unit radius. What is the largest constant $f(B^d) \in [0,1]$ with the property that every finite collection $\mathcal{C}$ of unit balls in $\mathbb{R}^d$ admits a disjoint sub-collection $\mathcal{S}$ occupying at least a fraction $f(B^d)$ of the volume of $\mathcal{C}$? This problem was first raised by T. Rad\'o in 1928, for axis-parallel squares in the plane; the author was motivated by a classical covering lemma in real analysis due to Vitali. The case of Euclidean balls was first considered by R. Rado in 1949.
  Until last year the best known estimates on $f(B^d)$ for unit balls where very far apart: \[ (1+\epsilon_d) 3^{-d} \leq f(B^d) \leq 2^{-d}, \] where $0<\epsilon_d=o_{d\rightarrow \infty}(1)$. Recently, the authors of this note observed that an exponential improvement on the upper bound follows from the Kabatiansky--Levenshtein spherical code bound, while the lower bound was improved by a linear factor by C.~Xie and G.~Ge (see arxiv:2608.09744). The current best estimates for large $d$ are \[ c \cdot d \cdot 3^{-d} \leq f(B^d) \leq 2.447^{-d}, \] where $c>0$ is an absolute constant. Here we offer the first exponential improvement of the lower bound in almost 80 years, which narrows the gap to:
  \[ 2.910^{-d} \leq f(B^d) \leq 2.447^{-d}. \] Our method is constructive and yields a polynomial time algorithm for finding a disjoint sub-collection realizing the estimate. Moreover the same technique gives similar exponentially improved lower bounds for all symmetric convex bodies satisfying a uniform convexity assumption, e.g., $\ell^p$-balls for all $p\in (1,\infty)$.

papers.title: Chern Holomorphic Sectional Curvature: Canonical Ampleness, Rigidity, and Flatness Counterexamples
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a compact Brody-hyperbolic complex manifold admitting a strictly positive real $(1,1)$-current $T$ with smooth $dT$ and $dd^cT\le0$. We prove that the canonical bundle $K_X$ of $X$ is nef. If every positive Lelong level set of $T$ has complex dimension at most two, then $K_X$ is ample and $X$ admits a smooth plurinegative Hermitian metric. Strictly negative Chern holomorphic sectional curvature implies Brody hyperbolicity and, when constant, forces the given metric to be K\"ahler under the latter current hypotheses. We also establish K\"ahlerness for nonpositive constant Chern holomorphic sectional curvature in Fujiki's class, and for nonzero constant curvature on compact complex threefolds and compact balanced fourfolds. In every complex dimension at least seven, we construct compact balanced metrics with zero Chern holomorphic sectional curvature, nonzero Chern curvature, vanishing of all four Chern--Ricci contractions, and a nowhere-vanishing Chern-parallel holomorphic volume form. Finally, for compact Hermitian manifolds with zero Chern holomorphic sectional curvature and vanishing first Chern--Ricci tensor, a smooth semipositive plurinegative $(1,1)$-form, positive definite at one point, forces the metric to be K\"ahler flat.

papers.title: Twisted Patterson-Sullivan densities on nilpotent covers for Anosov subgroups
papers.abstract: Let $\Gamma<\mathsf{SL}(d,\mathbb R)$ be a torsion-free, Zariski-dense Borel-Anosov subgroup, and let $\varphi$ be a linear functional positive on the limit cone of $\Gamma$. For every $\chi \in \operatorname{Hom}(\Gamma, \mathbb R)$, we construct twisted $(\varphi,\chi)$-conformal densities and prove their existence, uniqueness and ergodicity. For every non-trivial normal subgroup $\Gamma_0\lhd\Gamma$ with nilpotent quotient, we classify the ergodic $\varphi$-conformal densities of $\Gamma_0$ in terms of characters of $\Gamma/\Gamma_0$. Up to scaling, they are naturally parametrized by $\operatorname{Hom}(\Gamma/\Gamma_0,\mathbb R)$, and their dimensions are precisely the critical exponents of the corresponding twisted Poincar\'e series. We also prove a shadow lemma for twisted densities of normal subgroups, with estimates uniform over densities with fixed parameters, and a twisted Hopf-Tsuji-Sullivan theorem.

papers.title: Equivariant bordism rigidity for toric manifolds
papers.authors: Runze Chen, Yuanxin Guan, Zhi L\"{u}
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a bordism-theoretic approach to rigidity problems for toric and quasitoric manifolds. We prove that two toric manifolds are isomorphic as varieties if and only if they are weakly equivariantly unitary bordant. We also establish a parallel rigidity result for omnioriented quasitoric manifolds satisfying the injectivity condition, showing that their equivariant unitary bordism classes completely determine their omniorientation-preserving equivariant homeomorphism types. Thus, equivariant bordism provides a topological framework for detecting geometric and combinatorial rigidity.

papers.title: Chromatic Extremal Thresholds and the Multipartite $K_4$-Free Problem
papers.abstract: For positive integers $n,r,t$, let $\delta(n,r,t)$ denote the maximum possible minimum degree of a balanced $r$-partite graph with parts of size $n$ and chromatic number at most $t$. Lo, Treglown and Zhao established a general upper bound for this parameter and used it, together with explicit constructions, to determine the corresponding multipartite clique threshold up to an additive constant in a broad parameter range. I determine the chromatic parameter throughout the range $r=mt-a$, $m\ge2$, $t\ge3$, $2\le a\le \min\{m,t-1\}$. The answer differs from the Lo--Treglown--Zhao upper bound by at most one. I give an explicit arithmetic criterion deciding when this one-unit correction occurs. The proof reduces the problem to an integer matrix extremum. In the boundary case, equality forces the supports of all mixed rows to form a spanning star, after which the only remaining obstruction is a divisibility condition. Combining this formula with the Andrasfai--Erdos--Sos theorem sharpens the known equality range for $f(n,r,t+1)=\delta(n,r,t)$. In particular, for $t=3$ it removes the remaining size restrictions at $r=10$ and $r=13$. Together with the $r=7$ result in arXiv:2609.19177, the classical $r=4$ case, and the known congruence classes, this gives a formula for the multipartite $K_4$-free problem for every admissible $r\ge4$ and every $n\ge1$.

papers.title: Searching Schemes With $p$-Adic Neumann Boundary Value Problems
papers.abstract: Firstly, for branched covering maps $f\colon Y\to X$ between smooth, separated schemes of finite type over the integral ring $O_K$ of a non-archimedean local field $K$, the ramification divisor is found to coincide with the divisor of the Radon-Nikodym derivative of the Radon measure associated with an algebraic differential form on $Y$ against the pullback measure of one on $X$, both taking Borel sets of the space $Y(O_K)$ of $O_K$-rational points of $Y$ as input values. Secondly, the ultracontractivity of semigroups generated by Laplacian integral operators having a geodetic-distance-power kernel function is proven, using heat kernel estimates for ultrametric operators on $p$-adic balls. Thirdly, a series of $p$-adic Neumann Boundary Value Problems, depending on algebraic and pluricanonical differential forms with poles on spaces $X(O_K)$ coming from schemes is formulated and solved, extending previous work of the author. These results are then used to solve reconstruction problems on schemes: the divisor of a pluricanonical form with poles with at worst log-terminal singularities, as well as Weierstrass points of projective algebraic curves can be reconstructed via repeatedly finding weak solutions of $p$-adic Neumann Boundary Value Problems.

papers.title: Positive scalar curvature K\"ahler cones on compact complex surfaces
papers.abstract: We determine the positive scalar curvature K\"ahler cone of every minimal compact K\"ahler surface of Kodaira dimension $-\infty$. By the Enriques--Kodaira classification, every such surface is either $\mathbb P^2$ or a geometrically ruled surface $\mathbb P(E)\to\Sigma_g$, where $E$ is a rank-two holomorphic vector bundle over a compact Riemann surface of genus $g$. On $\mathbb P^2$, every K\"ahler class admits a K\"ahler metric of positive scalar curvature, whereas on $\mathbb P(E)$, every K\"ahler class of positive total scalar curvature admits a metric of positive scalar curvature if and only if $g\le1$ or $E$ is slope-semistable. We further prove that if a smooth compact K\"ahler surface admits a birational morphism onto a ruled surface $\mathbb P(E)\to\Sigma_g$, where $g\ge2$ and $E$ is slope-unstable, then it contains a K\"ahler class of positive total scalar curvature admitting no positive scalar curvature K\"ahler metric. Finally, for every smooth compact K\"ahler surface $X$ birational to $Y=\mathbb P^2$ or $Y=\mathbb P(E)$, we show that K\"ahler classes admitting positive scalar curvature metrics on $Y$ are exactly the pushforwards of classes admitting such metrics on $X$.

papers.title: Resilient forest universality in percolated dense graphs
papers.abstract: Christoph, M\"uyesser and Wigderson recently asked whether an approximate form of the Erd\H{o}s-S\'os conjecture is robust under random edge deletions. We establish a density-sensitive transference theorem that converts global resilience for bounded-degree trees in sparse random graphs into resilient forest universality in arbitrary dense host graphs. More precisely, if $F$ is an $N$-vertex graph of edge density $\lambda$ bounded away from zero and $p\in[K/N,1]$, then, with probability $1-o(1)$ uniformly over the host and the percolation parameter, every subgraph obtained from $F_p$ by deleting at most an $\alpha$-fraction of its edges contains every bounded-degree forest on at most $((1-\alpha)\lambda-\xi)N$ vertices. Consequently, for every $c>0$, $L\ge1$, fixed $D$ and $\alpha<c$, every graph $F$ on at most $Ld$ vertices with average degree at least $d$ has the property that, after percolation at any rate $p\in[K/d,1]$ and any subsequent deletion of at most an $\alpha$-fraction of the surviving edges, the remaining graph is universal for all forests on at most $(1-c)d$ vertices and maximum degree at most $D$. This includes vertex-disjoint packings of any prescribed collection of bounded-degree trees of that total order. We further obtain forest-universality results for graphs whose connected components have vertex-cover number at most $Cd$, and for graphs that can be brought into this form by deleting sufficiently few edges on the $dn$-scale.

papers.title: Second-Order Stationarity with Common Random Losses: Matching Tolerance Bounds
papers.authors: Wendao Wu, Haihan Zhang, Chenheng Zhang, Yanyi Li, Chunyuan Zheng, Cong Fang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin
papers.abstract:
We establish tight polynomial tolerance bounds for stochastic second-order stationarity when each fresh oracle response is a derivative of one common random scalar loss. For a population objective $F$ with Lipschitz gradient and Hessian, the target is $\|
abla F(x)\|\le \epsilon$ and $\lambda_{\min}(
abla^2 F(x))\ge -\gamma$, with independent tolerances $\epsilon,\gamma>0$. Under bounded gradient variance and almost-surely bounded Hessian error, the minimax number of fresh gradient or Hessian-vector-product calls is $\widetilde{\Theta}\!\left(\epsilon^{-3}+\gamma^{-5}ight)$. The characterization fixes positive gap, smoothness, and noise parameters, suppresses logarithmic factors, and allows dimension to grow within an explicit polynomial envelope. The upper bound removes the mixed term $\epsilon^{-2}\gamma^{-2}$ from the earlier fresh-HVP guarantee. Direct random-line Hessian estimates and a dyadic gradient tracker separate gradient drift from randomly signed curvature motion. The lower bound realizes the endpoint costs through globally defined smooth random losses: a smooth partition localizes scalar noise without a chain-length penalty, while exact cancellation limits the information in the entire response. Consequently, the same tolerance exponents hold even for joint value, gradient, and full-Hessian responses with bounded value variance. For a population Hessian with H"older exponent $
u\in(0,1]$, fresh gradient/HVP complexity becomes $\widetilde{\Theta}\!\left(\epsilon^{-3}+\gamma^{-(3+2/
u)}ight)$ under the corresponding dimension envelope.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Higher-Order Oracle Complexity for Convex--Concave Minimax Optimization
papers.authors: Yanyi Li, Haihan Zhang, Chenheng Zhang, Wendao Wu, Chunyuan Zheng, Cong Fang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin
papers.abstract: For smooth convex--concave minimax optimization, the higher-order lower bound of Chen et al. (2026) applies to a restricted tensor-algorithm class with prescribed regularized Taylor-model updates. We establish the same bound for arbitrary adaptive deterministic and randomized algorithms, matching, up to logarithmic factors, the upper bound of Zhang et al. (2026). Fix an integer $p\ge 2$ and let $L_p>0$ bound the Lipschitz constant of the objective's $p$-th derivative on a compact convex product domain of diameter at most $D_Z>0$. Each feasible query returns the objective value and all derivatives through order $p$. For accuracy $\epsilon>0$, set $Q_{\mathrm{tan}}=L_pD_Z^p/\epsilon$ for tangent residual and $Q_{\mathrm{gap}}=L_pD_Z^{p+1}/\epsilon$ for saddle gap. Let $T_E^{\mathrm{det}}(\epsilon)$ and $T_E^{\mathrm{rand}}(\epsilon)$ denote the high-dimensional minimax query complexities for criterion $E\in\{\mathrm{tan},\mathrm{gap}\}$, with randomized success probability at least $2/3$ on every instance. Our lower bounds and the existing upper bound give $c_pQ_E^{2/(3p-1)}\le T_E^{\mathrm{rand}}(\epsilon)\le T_E^{\mathrm{det}}(\epsilon)\le C_pQ_E^{2/(3p-1)}[1+\log(3+Q_E)]^{6(p-1)}$ for sufficiently large $Q_E$, where $c_p,C_p>0$ depend only on $p$. Thus the same accuracy exponent holds beyond tensor update rules, even for randomized queries and arbitrary feasible outputs. The proof constructs a scalar convex--concave chain with exactly flat gates that hide complete derivative information. Direct product-domain error witnesses and adaptive transcript arguments establish the lower bounds for both criteria.

papers.title: DC decompositions and cutting-plane approximation: geometry and complexity
papers.abstract: We study how Difference of Convex (DC) decomposition affects cutting-plane approximation in global optimization. For a smooth decomposition $f = g-h$, let $d$ be the dimension of the span of all Hessian ranges of $g$ over the convex hull of a compact feasible set. The smallest attainable dimension equals the minimum rank of a constant positive semidefinite matrix majorizing the Hessians of $f$ on that convex hull, and is attained by a quadratic first component. Retaining earlier gradient cuts and accepting new cuts only when the model error exceeds $\epsilon$ gives an $O(\epsilon^{-d/2})$ bound on accepted cuts. For an adaptive global DC method, this also bounds the number of subproblems solved exactly and globally. Under nondegeneracy, the exponent is sharp for uniform cutting-plane approximation of quadratic first components. A structured example reduces the certified exponent from $n/2$ to $1/2$ and the global subproblem to one variable.

papers.title: Blow-up for a semilinear Tricomi equation in the oscillatory regime at the critical Strauss-type exponent
papers.authors: Diego Marcon, Wanderley Nunes do Nascimento, Matheus C. Santos
papers.abstract: We study finite-time blow-up for a semilinear shifted Tricomi equation with decreasing propagation speed and an oscillatory scale-invariant mass. We focus on the Strauss-type critical regime and prove that every weak solution with finite speed of propagation, arising from nonnegative nontrivial energy data satisfying a suitable localization condition, blows up in finite time. For sufficiently small initial data, we also obtain the corresponding critical exponential upper bound for the lifespan. The proof relies on a positive self-similar solution of the homogeneous adjoint equation represented by the Gauss hypergeometric function. Combined with a previously established lower bound for the nonlinear term and new estimates adapted to the critical case, this construction reduces the PDE problem to a nonlinear differential inequality. An ODE comparison argument then yields both finite-time blow-up and the lifespan estimate.

papers.title: Proper scoring rules for survival times
papers.abstract: This note presents a general form for a proper scoring rule that can be used for possibly right-censored survival data without requiring any knowledge or assumptions about the censoring process, so long as it is independent of survival time.

papers.title: Global well-posedness of defocusing cubic NLS in $M^{\infty,1}(\mathbb{R})$
papers.abstract: We prove global well-posedness of the one-dimensional defocusing cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation in the modulation space $M^{\infty,1}(\mathbb{R})$. This space imposes no spatial decay and contains $C_b^2(\mathbb{R})$ as well as all absolutely convergent sums of plane waves. The result applies to arbitrary data in this space, including large smooth quasiperiodic profiles and their localized perturbations. The proof constructs a nonnegative density satisfying a local conservation law from forward Weyl ratios, which are defined through half-line square-integrable solutions of the associated spectral problem. A suitable nonlinear combination of localized integrals of this density controls the modulation norm. Finally, choosing the spatial localization scale and NLS scaling in a coordinated way makes the accumulated boundary flux small enough to continue every mild solution globally.

papers.title: On the Regularity and Clean Properties of Matrices over Dual Numbers
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study regularity and clean-type decompositions for matrices over dual numbers. We characterize the von Neumann regularity of dual matrices by establishing a necessary and sufficient compatibility condition between their real and dual components. At the element level, we determine the conditions under which an individual dual matrix $\mathcal{M} = A + B\epsilon$ is regular, $\pi$-regular, nil-clean, or strongly nil-clean. Using the solvability of Sylvester matrix equations, we show that the matrix ring over dual numbers $M_n(\mathbb{D})$ is strongly $\pi$-regular and strongly clean. Moreover, $M_n(\mathbb{D})$ is $\pi$-regular, clean, $r$-clean, strongly $r$-clean, $\mathrm{NR}$-clean, and strongly $\mathrm{NR}$-clean. On the other hand, $M_n(\mathbb{D})$ fails to be regular, strongly regular, nil-clean, strongly nil-clean, and uniquely $\mathrm{NR}$-clean, although it inherits several strong decomposition properties from $M_n(\mathbb{R})$. Our characterizations at the element level show exactly when each property holds.

papers.title: KAYROS: An Anytime and Exact Solver for the Time-Dependent Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows - Extended Version
papers.authors: Florian Rascoussier, Romain Billot, Lina Fahed, Christine Solnon
papers.abstract: The Time-Dependent Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows (TDVRPTW) captures a central difficulty of urban logistics: travel times vary with the time of day, so the cost of a route depends on when it is driven. This paper introduces KAYROS, an open-source solver for the duration-minimization TDVRPTW that is both anytime and exact. It returns improving valid solutions throughout its time budget and can close instances with conditional computational optimality certificates through an integrated branch-price-and-cut component. We extend the composition of continuous arrival-time functions from the literature, previously described only at proof or proposition level, to the left-continuous functions that stepwise benchmarks require. We prove that the composition routine shipped in the checker computes that operation exactly. We analyze when its evaluation and breakpoint normalization are exact in IEEE-754 double-precision arithmetic, and argue that a canonical, epsilon-free checker must define the objective.
